AI Search.description: Adds an AI search bar to the Jellyfin web client. Ask in natural language and get titles from your own library, personalized to your watch history. Also adds meaning-based matches inside Jellyfin's own native search, alongside title matches. Works with any OpenAI-compatible model, with a local or remote retrieval source.
AI Search.overview: AI natural-language search & recommendations from your own library.

versions.changelog:
For Jellyfin 12. Fixes for the three open issues.

- Newer OpenAI models work now. They refuse `max_tokens` and only accept the default temperature, so the plugin switches to `max_completion_tokens` and drops the temperature on its own, then remembers it for that model. You can also pick the field in the settings ("Reply length limit field"). Fixes #4.
- You can exclude libraries from AI Search. Ticked libraries are left out of the index, the AI search popup and the AI matches in Jellyfin's search, but still show up in Jellyfin's normal title search. Fixes #3.
- Building the index with a model that gives no embeddings (a reranker, or llama.cpp with `--pooling rank`) now stops with a clear message saying so, instead of a JSON error. If only a few titles fail, the build skips them and tells you how many. Fixes #2.

For Jellyfin 12. Searching is much faster, and you can now see where each result comes from.

What's new:
- Jellyfin's own search no longer waits for AI Search. Title results show up right away.
- AI matches get their own "AI Search" row under Jellyfin's results, with a short reason under each title.
- If a chat model is set up, it writes a one-line reason for each AI match a few seconds later.
- The plugin speaks French or English. By default it follows each user's Jellyfin language, or you can pick one in the settings.
- The search model is loaded as soon as you open the search page, so the first search isn't slow anymore.
- Repeated searches are almost instant, and the AI popup no longer loads your whole library before searching.

Fixes:
- The search page no longer jumps up or down while results and reasons load.
- Opening the AI search button no longer scrolls the page back to the top.
- The search history list in the popup is back to its normal layout.
- Remote search works again for searches made with an API key.
- Search log files no longer start with a byte-order mark.

TV and mobile apps still get AI matches mixed into Jellyfin's results, waiting at most 2 seconds for them. Jellyfin 10.11 servers stay on 1.1.1.0.

For Jellyfin 12. Jellyfin's own search now also finds titles by meaning, shown in the usual Movies, Shows and Episodes rows after the title matches. New options: turn it on or off, only use it for searches that look like a sentence, limit how many matches it adds, hide the AI search button completely (native search only), and keep a log of every search for a few days so an admin or API key can collect them.

versions.changelog: v1.8.3.36: Library jobs wait out a busy AI service (HTTP 429/503, following Retry-After) instead of failing the whole video on one rejected frame. The AI service now explains why an Intel/AMD GPU is not used (render group ID mismatch; see /doctor and /status) and runs OpenVINO on its CPU device instead of silently falling back; that part is in the AI service and needs the 1.8.3.36 Docker image. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.35: The player button no longer needs write access to Jellyfin's web folder. The plugin adds its script to index.html as Jellyfin serves the page, so Windows installs (NetworkService), the Debian package, snaps and read-only containers get the button in every browser tab. Behind a Jellyfin base URL, the Lanczos, Anime4K and WebGPU real-time engines load again. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.34: Real-time upscaling starts again in the web client. Since v1.8.3.31 it refused every video with "Video color metadata unavailable", because Jellyfin 10.9 and later no longer put the playing item in the page address; the player now reads the item from the video's stream or the web client's playback request and checks the version that plays. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.33: Redesigned in-player menu and settings page. SDR videos (DVD/SD rips, untagged 10-bit) are no longer refused as HDR in real time or in library jobs; HDR batch output keeps the model's detail; Server AI hides stale frames during outages and falls back to Lanczos when the server cannot keep up. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.32: Native Jellyfin 12 build on .NET 10, aligned plugin/test dependencies, updated CI and ABI-aware release validation. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

versions.changelog: v2.4.2 'Genre and studio badges that count what you watched' - FIXED (#154, thanks @mattsigal for his first PR, with once-per-item counting by @camarigor): TV episodes now credit studio badges with their series' studios (It's Not TV, Auntie Beeb and Netflix and Watch only ever saw movies); TMDb composite genres count for each part ('Action & Adventure' for Action Hero, 'Sci-Fi & Fantasy' for Sci-Fi Scholar and Fantasy Forever) and 'Sci-Fi' counts as 'Science Fiction'; studios match as a whole word plus aliases ('Walt Disney Pictures' counts for Disney, 'HBO Max' for HBO); every item counts once per badge however many of its names match. WHEN YOU UPDATE: watches already in your history start counting, so progress jumps and badges can unlock on the spot (on our server: 11 genre badges across 23 profiles, no progress went down); custom genre and studio badges match the same way (a custom 'War' badge now counts 'War & Politics'); episode plays from before this update stored no studio, so TV credit on studio badges starts now. FIXED (#147, @Roboatlas21, by @camarigor): the Friends chat's message box no longer sits behind a phone's navigation bar. CHANGED (#146, @Roboatlas21, by @camarigor): a plugin card image that survives the catalogue's crop. Deps: codeql-action 4.38.2, ClusterFuzzLite base image. 440/440 tests on both frameworks; smoke-tested on Jellyfin 10.11.10 and 12.1.0. Sigstore-signed + SLSA attested. Drop-in from v2.4.x - no migration.

v2.4.1 'What 2.4.0 got wrong, and a cap you can raise' - FIXED (#140, @Roboatlas21): the Jellyfin 12 package reported a version Jellyfin could not act on. Both assemblies were stamped x.y.z.0, so the dashboard showed 2.4.0.0 for an install the manifest called 2.4.0.1 - the plugin image 404'd and UNINSTALL FAILED OUTRIGHT. Each package now stamps the version it ships as. Stuck on 2.4.0.1? Updating through the catalogue is enough; the restart that loads the new build removes the old folder. FIXED (#141, @Roboatlas21): the page worked in a private window and nowhere else. A browser that cached Jellyfin's page before the plugin was installed revalidates it, Jellyfin answers 304 from the file on disk, and a 304 has no body to inject into - so the browser kept using a copy with no plugin in it. Worst where the web directory is read-only, since the on-disk patch cannot take either. The middleware now forces a full page while the patch has not taken. No need to clear browsing data; a normal reload is enough. CHANGED (#129, @Tschiyo): the targeted badge cap is a setting, 1 to 1000, default still 50, with the targets past it named on the page; the per-play check no longer grows with the target count (ancestor-set lookup, cached collection/playlist members). FIXED (#133, @clarjon1): the Revamp style reached the rest of Jellyfin - invisible checkboxes, text inputs losing border and height, selection colour changing everywhere, on Jellyfin's own controls and every other plugin's settings page. Twelve rules are now anchored to this plugin's own surfaces. FIXED (#131, @Borededdy): a Custom Tab rendered nothing under a theme that ships its own copy of Jellyfin's home page (Abyss); the plugin now builds the missing panel itself. NEW (#136, @Verdancy-Rin): a top-center toast placement plus an admin default for users who have not picked one; also fixed - the default UI style (#43) was never stored, and every main config save switched the page integrations back off. NEW (#138, @Digital-Yeti): optional, off by default - keep accounts hidden from Jellyfin's login screen out of other users' leaderboards, activity feed, friend search, compare picker and profile endpoints. FIXED: this plugin had been returning 500 for the whole server's /api-docs/openapi.json since 2.1.0 - its MediaType enum collided with Jellyfin's own type name and took the entire OpenAPI document down, breaking Swagger UI and every spec-driven client, silently. Renamed to BadgeMediaType; numbers and property names unchanged, nothing to migrate. 421/421 tests on both frameworks; verified live on Jellyfin 10.11.10 and 12.1.0. Sigstore-signed + SLSA attested. Drop-in from v2.4.0 - no schema change, no migration.

v2.4.0 'Jellyfin 12, targeted badges, games' - JELLYFIN 12 (#109): every release now ships two packages, x.y.z.0 for Jellyfin 10.11 (.NET 9) and x.y.z.1 for Jellyfin 12 (.NET 10); the catalog picks the right one. On 12 the Achievements entry is in the avatar menu below Profile, the equipped strip sits in the toolbar, every call sends the Authorization header 12 requires (legacy X-Emby-Token alone answers 401), the Revamp admin page fits the MUI dashboard, links use #/ routes. Thanks @camarigor (#117, #122, #128) and @Lyxon1337. NEW: targeted badges (#107) - ContainerCompletionPercent and ItemPlayCount point a badge at one series, season, collection, playlist, album or item via a library picker; retroactive on creation. NEW: JellyEmu game achievements (#115) - nine built-in badges and three custom metrics. NEW (#42): everything you equip in the shop - custom title, badge frame, profile theme, profile border, animated background, avatar - now shows on all three shareable-card skins and on the friends-drawer card. FIXED: toast placement under Revamp (#116); Pastel 'un-hidden elements' (every gradient theme let Jellyfin's page show through); profile borders never showed under Revamp; badge frames were nearly invisible on the achievements page; the shop's 'Auto-unlock at N score' pill was clipped; ~25 Users/Me requests on the login page; the Revamp stylesheet cached under a stale token in three places; admin hero reported v1.9.2 forever. #97 diagnostics: reset returns 400/404 for bad ids, admin errors name the failing request, an empty scan points at library access. 306/306 tests on both frameworks, smoke-tested on Jellyfin 12.0.0 and 10.11.10. Sigstore-signed + SLSA attested. Drop-in from v2.3.x.

versions.changelog: Corretto il doppio caricamento dopo un aggiornamento (issue #2): lo ZIP contiene un meta.json con il nome del plugin, così Jellyfin tiene tutte le versioni sotto lo stesso nome e rimuove la vecchia, e all'avvio il plugin segna come superate le proprie copie più vecchie. Licenza AGPLv3 con termini aggiuntivi (attribuzione, versioni modificate riconoscibili, marchi e mascotte); attribuzione e link al codice sorgente nella pagina del plugin. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AniList come fonte senza chiave insieme a TMDB: cast giapponese con i personaggi, studio di animazione, date, stato, voto, trailer, copertina e banner, solo nei campi vuoti. L'anno di una stagione senza date arriva dalla catena dei sequel di AniList, se gli episodi coincidono. Gli ID AniList che non corrispondono per tipo o anno vengono ignorati. Nuovo passo AniList nel setup. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Comunità per tutti: dopo una correzione il plugin chiede se condividerla e la invia tramite il servizio della comunità, senza account; il token GitHub diventa facoltativo. Si condividono anche le stagioni con una scheda propria, applicate agli altri solo se numero di stagione ed episodi coincidono. Elenco approvato aggiornato ogni giorno, controlli automatici e approvazione con un'etichetta, tessera Comunità in Inizio, passo Comunità nel setup e scelta della stagione in «Correggi un abbinamento». Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Pagina del plugin rifatta da zero con l'identità di AnimeClick: setup guidato al primo avvio e solo i passi nuovi dopo gli aggiornamenti importanti, vetrina degli ultimi anime aggiornati, cruscotto della collezione, libreria a locandine con titoli e trame uniti per anime, attivazione delle librerie a un clic e ricerca della scheda su AnimeClick per correggere un abbinamento. Corretti i conteggi dell'analisi di una singola serie, lo stato della condivisione comunitaria appena attivata e «Da verificare», che ora coincide con quanto «Sistema tutti i titoli» ricontrolla. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Scarta i titoli alternativi di un'altra stagione verificando il titolo inglese originale. Quando manca una fonte coerente, traduce il titolo inglese già valido; esclude i nomi dei file. Correzione trovata sul NAS in anteprima, senza salvare la proposta errata. Include le novità 1.2.1. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AnimeClick come unico provider remoto per le librerie anime: identificazione TMDB verificata, completamento dei metadati senza altri plugin e immagini integrate Fanart → TMDB → AnimeClick. Chiavi Fanart personale e di progetto nelle impostazioni, con link e verifica. Numerazione, campi bloccati e immagini esistenti conservati. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

AnimeClick primo campo per campo: i valori generici lasciano spazio alle fonti configurate. Recupero italiano e traduzione dall’inglese anche per serie, film, generi e tag, senza mescolare titolo e trama. Le immagini conservano la precedenza dei provider ad alta risoluzione; nessun aggiornamento immagini o riparazione viene avviato dall’installazione. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Titoli episodio mancanti: ricerca su TheTVDB e TMDB configurati dopo AnimeClick, precedenza all’italiano e traduzione dei soli titoli inglesi con il profilo AI esistente. Verifica degli ID esterni, conservazione dei titoli compilati e indicazione della fonte nell’avanzamento. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

La tua libreria con analisi automatica, viste separate, avanzamento reale e interruzione dei lavori. Recupero dei soli titoli mancanti con protezione dei metadati esistenti. Abbinamenti della comunità e invio automatico delle correzioni su GitHub, entrambi facoltativi e disattivati di default. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo.

Major per Jellyfin 12 e .NET 10, verificata su 12.0 e 12.1. Interfaccia riprogettata con guida iniziale, preferenze semplici e strumenti avanzati separati. Identificazione automatica più prudente fra titoli simili, remake e stagioni; correzione manuale cercando il titolo in libreria e incollando il link AnimeClick, senza cancellazione diretta delle immagini. Corretti redirect di rete, collisioni e scadenza della cache, concorrenza nei refresh, rate limit e coerenza della coda traduzioni. AI opzionale e disattivabile senza perdere il profilo; impostazioni e credenziali esistenti conservate. 210 test backend per versione server e 11 test browser. Richiede Jellyfin 12.0 o successivo: non installare su 10.11; le release precedenti restano disponibili. Dettagli e limiti delle verifiche nel rapporto di audit della release.

Artwork Generator.description: Artwork Generator is a Jellyfin plugin that automatically creates custom episode posters using smart frame analysis, black frame detection, and configurable text styling. Perfect for filling in missing or generic episode artwork with clean, consistent visuals.

versions.changelog:
## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## Features
- Frames are no longer taken from inside media segments, so intros, credits, recaps, previews, and commercials stay out of generated artwork
- New Avoid Media Segments setting under Frame Extraction, with a checkbox for each kind of segment to avoid, all on by default
- Segments come from a media segment provider turned on for the library, so items without any extract as before

## Developer
- Changing which segments are avoided discards the idle frame pools, so the next refresh extracts under the new choice

## Features
- New Cleanup Backdrops scheduled task under Library that reduces every item on the server to a single backdrop, keeping the first and deleting the rest along with their files
- The task has no default schedule, so it only runs when started by hand or on a trigger you add

## Features
- Primary and thumb images can name a second and third design, adding their versions of the same frames to the Edit Images picker
- New Edit Images Cache setting for how long rendered choices stay available, default 30 minutes
- Edit Images reuses the choices it already rendered when switching image type or page, instead of rendering every image again

## Fixes
- The Edit Images cache is bounded by size at 256 MB and releases expired images on its own, instead of holding them until the next render
- Every design in one Edit Images render draws from the same frames, even while other items are extracting
- Posters pass over a logo Jellyfin only knows by web address and use the next logo that can be read

## Developer
- Settings saved before 12.0.2.0 are no longer brought forward, so update through 12.0.2.1 first when coming from an older version
- Code, pages, and docs say logo rather than series logo, since films draw their own

## Fixes
- The Profiles page loads again instead of failing on a backdrop setting that no longer exists
- Posters with a logo draw the logo selected for a film, season, or series instead of falling back to text

## Features
- Artwork Generator is Episode Poster Generator rebuilt, with the same settings and a much wider job
- The repository moved with the name; re-add it as jellyfin-plugin-artworkgenerator to keep getting updates
- Draws posters, thumbs, backdrops, and text logos, where before there were only episode posters
- Covers series, seasons, films, music videos, home videos, and anything else with a video
- Configuration is rebuilt in three parts, designs, logos, and profiles
- Profiles decide which items get which images and which design draws each one
- Every design renders portrait and landscape, so one design covers a tall poster and a wide thumb
- A design's two lines are now simply the title and the subtitle, whatever the item is
- Text position and alignment work on every design, not just the few that had them
- New Bloom design, pooling color from the frame behind the text
- New Grid canvas, tiling several extracted frames into one picture
- Logo designs build a text logo from any name field, with letter case, a line limit, and frame-filled letters
- Frame extraction is one set of server settings instead of a copy on every design
- Frames are ranked on tone, detail, contrast, and color rather than just clearing a threshold
- Optional setting drops a subtitle that only repeats the title
- A subtitle too long to fit can shorten to its code, shrink, or trim
- Two example designs per style, each showing a genuinely different look

## Fixes
- Seasons extract from their own episodes instead of falling back to the series backdrop
- Candidate images come from different episodes instead of clustering in one
- Heavily letterboxed frames scale back up to a usable size
- Portrait text is measured against both sides, so it no longer reads small
- Brush strokes stay thick on tall posters instead of piling into a cross
- Long titles trim at a word boundary rather than mid-word
- Descenders stay inside the safe area
- Borders, rules, and shadows scale with the poster
- A static graphic keeps its proportions
- An item with no name of its own says its one line in the larger type
- Generated images carry the item's metadata language

## Developer
- The generator, the settings model, and the configuration page are rebuilt around item kinds rather than episodes
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 that Jellyfin 12.0 ships
- Designs are found by reflection, so adding one needs a class and an enum value
- Every label, option, and default is read from the settings models
- The shared generator is split into pipeline, text, and overlay
- Frame analysis is a single pass, under a megabyte per frame instead of three and a half
- Every one-time upgrade of an older configuration sits in its own file, to be deleted whole once installs have moved on
- Tests hold the documentation, the templates, and US spelling to the code

## Features
- Shadows, rules, and the Frame border now scale with the poster, so they read the same on a 4K frame as on a DVD rip instead of turning into a hairline or a slab
- Long titles that do not fit two lines fill the first line with whole words and trim only the second, at a word boundary, instead of cutting both lines mid-word

## Fixes
- Frame drew no border at all for an episode without a name, and ignored the Show Title setting
- Cutout no longer lets a two line title run into the bottom of the cutout letters
- Split center-crops the series poster into its panel instead of stretching artwork that is not 2:3
- Brush honours the Show Episode setting and keeps a wrapped title inside the area the strokes leave clear
- Timeline keeps the marker dot inside the safe area on the first and last episode
- Text blocks are reserved from the font's real ascent and descent, so descenders no longer hang past the safe area

## Developer
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 packages Jellyfin 12.0 ships, since the plugin binds to the server's copies at runtime
- Text drawing moved from the removed SKPaint text members to SKFont, wrapped in a shared TextStyle so every style measures and draws with the same objects
- Standard and Split share one text stack; Numeral, Cutout, Brush, and Frame no longer hand-build their own paints
- Cutout renders through a canvas layer instead of a full-size scratch bitmap per poster; Split and Brush dispose their gradient shaders
- Letterbox detection scans the pixel buffer directly instead of a native call per pixel
- Bitmap scaling uses explicit cubic resampling now that FilterQuality is gone

## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

versions.changelog: An **animated GIF background now also moves in the live preview in Firefox**. It only moved in Chrome, Edge and other Chromium-based browsers before; Firefox kept showing a single frame. The preview now plays the GIF in real time at its own speed, redrawn up to about 15 times a second (very fast GIFs skip frames in the preview to keep time). Covers you applied were never affected: they always animated. Browsers that cannot decode an image frame by frame (Safari, for example) still show a still preview, but the applied cover animates as usual.

A polish release for the editor, driven by a full review of the page. **Spacing is fixed**: since the guided-steps redesign some controls sat flush against each other (the Restore button touched the Type dropdown, *In context* touched Dimensions) while other gaps were twice as big. Every step now has one even rhythm, and dropdowns line up with the buttons beside them. **Errors are readable**: when the server refuses a request you now see why — your session expired, the file is too large, too many requests, or the server's own reason for refusing a design — in your own language, instead of *"Unexpected end of JSON input"*, and nothing is left stuck on "Applying…". **Fewer surprises**: Restore, deleting a template and batch apply now ask before they act (like Reset backup already did), batch apply says how many covers it will replace and can no longer be started twice, loading a template asks before replacing changes you have not applied, and the browser warns before you close the tab with unapplied work — only when the design really differs from what you last applied, saved or loaded. Undo and loading a template **keep your background image** on the preview instead of dropping it, and an animated GIF background keeps moving. Choosing a **Custom** size or **Animated GIF** now shows their settings straight away, and **Save this design** and **Apply to several targets** are no longer tucked away under Advanced. Custom sizes stay between 100 and 2048 pixels, which is what the server accepts. The editor now **works from the keyboard and with a screen reader**: select layers with Tab and Enter, move the selected layer with the arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps; Alt, Ctrl and Meta combinations are left to the browser), and use the poster browser as a proper dialog that Esc closes and that keeps keyboard focus inside while you page through posters. Every icon button has a name. The poster browser follows **light themes** and the Jellyfin theme colours too. On narrow screens the layer **⋯** button works again. The title starts as the name of the target you pick, the Apply button says what it applies to (library, collection, playlist or Live TV), and switching the display language back to English no longer leaves Dutch or Spanish labels behind. Ctrl+Z now also undoes a slider or colour change, and is no longer intercepted on other dashboard pages. Existing designs and saved templates are unaffected and render exactly as before.

The live preview and the cover that actually gets applied now **agree on text effects**. A **shadow's softness** came out twice as wide on the applied cover as in the preview; it now matches, so a cover with a blurred text shadow looks slightly sharper than before once you apply it again. An **outline on semi-transparent text** used to stay fully solid on the cover however far you turned the opacity down; it now fades with the text, as the preview always showed, and outline corners are a little rounder. On **rotated text**, the cover turned the shadow along with the letters while the preview kept it falling the same way on screen; the cover now does what the preview shows. The preview itself had a few slips of its own: semi-transparent text with a shadow was drawn **slightly too dense**, the **in-context previews** (wide, square, poster) drew text, shadow and outline at full size so they spilled out of the little thumbnails, an **uploaded font** looked artificially bold when the weight was set to bold (the cover never was), and a **gradient from an old template** with fewer than two colour stops showed different colours in the editor, the preview and the cover. All three now show the same colours. Covers you have already applied are not changed until you apply them again. Fully opaque, unrotated text without a blurred shadow or an outline looks the same as before.

A **fix-up release for backups and the live preview**.
**Applying a cover a second time could be refused** with *"Could not back up the current cover"* on libraries that had no backup before 4.0.2.0. The backup was saved under one spelling of the library's id and looked for under another. Backups made by earlier versions are found again, so they keep working and the refusals stop.
**Covers made by this plugin are no longer saved as the "original".** The plugin now remembers the cover it applied last and never backs that up, nor anything in its own data folder. A backup is no longer made of a cover the plugin applied. If you applied covers with an earlier version before a target's first backup was taken (while trying the plugin out, for example), that backup may hold one of those test covers, and **Restore original cover** brings the test cover back instead of the real original. Covers applied by 4.0.2.0 are not recognised as plugin covers until you have applied once with this version.
The new **Reset backup** button next to Restore deletes a target's backup. It saves nothing itself: the next apply stores the cover the target shows at that moment as the new original, unless it is a cover the plugin applied. To fix a wrong backup, first put the cover you want to keep back on the library: upload it in Jellyfin (**Edit images** in the dashboard), or delete the poster and refresh metadata with *Replace existing images*. Then press **Reset backup**, then apply. This matters most if your old backup holds an early test cover, because your true original was overwritten before backups existed and has to come from you. Restores, backups and skipped backups are now written to the Jellyfin log.
In the editor, a **poster collage** background now shows in the live preview. It used to stay black until you pressed Show server render. An **animated GIF** background now moves in the preview instead of standing still, unless your system is set to reduce motion.

A **hardening and housekeeping** release — apart from the fixes below, nothing about how you design covers changes. Applied covers now go through **Jellyfin's own image handling**, the same path as uploading an image in the dashboard, so they are stored alongside the rest of your library artwork and, for covers applied or restored from this version on, **keep working even if the plugin's data folder is cleared** (covers applied by 4.0.1.0 and never re-applied still live in that folder); **Restore original cover** works exactly as before. If the current cover cannot be backed up first, applying is now **refused with a clear message** and the cover is left untouched, so the cover you had before you first used the plugin can always be restored (a cover you set in the dashboard after an earlier apply is replaced by the next apply, as with Jellyfin's own upload). A logo or icon layer scaled larger than **1.5× the canvas** now renders at most 1.5×, so old templates with huge logos render smaller. **Animated images are handled far more carefully**: the server only ever decodes the frames it actually needs (one for a still cover, at most 60 for an animated one). A long or high-resolution animated GIF is no longer turned away — the plugin simply uses as many of its frames as fit safely in memory — and only an image whose single frame is larger than 8192×8192 pixels is **refused at upload with a clear message**. **Ken Burns** covers no longer **stretch** a background whose shape differs from the cover, animated covers render faster, and a shrunk animated GIF keeps its blur and border in proportion. A single faulty text layer can no longer **blank out the whole cover** — it is skipped and everything else still renders. Size errors such as *"Dimensions too large"* are now shown as they are instead of a generic failure. Behind the scenes, the applied-cover folder no longer grows with every apply, applying to the same library or collection is now done one at a time so two applies can no longer overwrite each other, rapid repeated requests can no longer slip past the rate limits (rejected uploads now count toward the upload limit too), and saving a template while a batch apply runs is now safe. **TIFF uploads are no longer accepted** — browsers cannot draw TIFF in the editor, so they never previewed properly; convert to PNG or JPG. The background upload limit can now be changed with `MaxUploadSizeMb` in the plugin's configuration file (1–50 MB, default 5); values above about 28 MB may still be blocked earlier by the web server's own request-size limit.

Fixes the configuration page on Jellyfin 12, where **nothing worked**. Jellyfin 12 stopped accepting the older of its two ways of proving who you are, and the page was still using it — so every request it made was rejected before it reached the plugin. Libraries did not load, saved templates did not appear, the bundled fonts did not arrive, applying a cover did nothing, and opening the poster browser produced the cryptic message *"Failed to execute 'json' on 'Response': Unexpected end of JSON input"*, which was the rejection with no explanation attached. The page now identifies itself the same way the Jellyfin web client does, which works on Jellyfin 10.11 and 12 alike. **If you installed 4.0.0.0, update** — nothing was wrong with your settings or your covers, the page simply could not reach the server.

**Support for Jellyfin 12.** Jellyfin 12 moved to .NET 10 and changed its plugin ABI, so a plugin built for 10.11 cannot be built for both — this release is built against Jellyfin 12 and requires it. Nothing about designing or rendering covers has changed: your saved templates, applied covers and settings all carry over untouched. If you are **still on Jellyfin 10.11**, stay on **3.5.1.0** — your server will keep being offered that version and will not see this one, so nothing breaks by leaving it alone.

# 🚀 A New Foundation for File Transformation File Transformation **3.0.0.0** is a major overhaul of how the plugin integrates with Jellyfin. The transformation system has been rebuilt around standard ASP.NET Core middleware, removing much of the version-specific runtime patching that File Transformation previously relied on. Alongside **Jellyfin 12 support**, this release drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7** and lays a much more maintainable foundation for future Jellyfin releases. > ## 🙌 Huge thanks to @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv > > A massive part of this release is thanks to **@4eh5xitv6787h645ebv**, who took on the major overhaul of File Transformation's core architecture in PR #58. > > The move away from the old Harmony/MonoMod-based interception system to standard ASP.NET Core middleware is a significant piece of work. It not only makes File Transformation substantially easier to maintain, but also resolves an entire class of compatibility problems that caused the plugin to malfunction or be disabled on certain Jellyfin versions and platforms (#20, #35, #62, #64, #70, #71). > > This is far more than a small patch or isolated feature - it fundamentally improves the foundation the plugin is built on. A huge thank you for the time and effort that went into it. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and the newer Jellyfin server architecture (#34). * Replaced the previous Harmony/MonoMod-based web interception system with standard ASP.NET Core `IStartupFilter` middleware (PR #58, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv). * Added support for unregistering transformations through `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing dependent plugins to cleanly remove transformations when required. * Added support for synthesising virtual files for registered transformation paths, restoring support for plugins such as Plugin Pages where the underlying file doesn't physically exist. * Added ETag generation and `304 Not Modified` support for transformed content. * Added Brotli and gzip recompression of transformed responses for remote clients. * Added automatic MIME type detection for virtual transformed files. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Removed platform-specific DLL extraction and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * Removed dependencies on Harmony, MonoMod and Prometheus from the core transformation pipeline. * Improved compatibility across Jellyfin versions and platforms by moving the transformation system onto standard ASP.NET Core APIs (#20, #35, #62, #64). * Added per-transformation error isolation so a failure in one plugin's transformation won't prevent other transformations from running. * Made transformation registration, removal and execution thread-safe. * Added regex caching and timeout protection for transformation matching. * Improved handling of `Accept-Encoding`, including proper quality-value (`q`) parsing. * Improved LAN detection for IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses. * Improved proxy caching behaviour by correctly setting `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. * Reworked HTTP handling to use a shared `HttpClient` with appropriate timeouts. * Hardened named-pipe transformations with timeouts, size limits, EOF handling and improved resource cleanup. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed a class of failures where Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching could cause File Transformation to malfunction or be automatically disabled on startup (#20, #35, #62, #64, #71). * Fixed #70 where transformations could attempt to use a disposed `IServiceProvider` after Jellyfin restarted, resulting in `500` responses across the web UI. * Fixed transformed content potentially retaining stale trailing bytes when a transformation produced a shorter result than the original response. * Fixed failures in one transformation potentially breaking the entire transformation pipeline. * Fixed potential `HttpClient` resource leaks. * Fixed named-pipe transformations being able to hang indefinitely or loop on zero-byte reads. * Fixed incorrect handling of disabled compression encodings such as `gzip;q=0`. * Fixed failed virtual-file transformations returning an empty successful response instead of reverting to the original `404`. * Improved middleware failure handling so the original response is served if transformation or recompression fails. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The existing `PluginInterface.RegisterTransformation` API and registration payload remain compatible with previous releases, so plugins using a standard transformation callback **should not need to change how they register transformations**. There are, however, some changes to transformation execution that plugin developers should be aware of: * Added `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing plugins to explicitly unregister a previously registered transformation. * Assembly callbacks still receive the same payload and are expected to return the transformed content as a `string`. * Invalid or failed assembly callbacks now **fail safely rather than falling through to another configured callback mechanism**. Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

versions.changelog:
Afspil-knappen følger temaets egne farver - på ElegantFin lysegrå med sort tekst - i stedet for Jellyfins blå, også mens temaet indlæses.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Forsiden hentes meget hurtigere.

- Alle otte baggrunde blev hentet på én gang i 1920 gange skærmens pixeltæthed - 2880 px på en almindelig bærbar og 3,5 MB, mens forsiden stadig var ved at indlæse. Nu hentes kun det slide, der vises, og det næste, i en størrelse der passer til skærmen.
- Logoerne hentes også først, når deres slide er på vej.
- Indtil baggrunden er hentet, vises en sløret udgave af den.
- Størrelserne er dem, New Badges 2.8.2.0 laver på forhånd på serveren, så billederne kommer med det samme.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Intet blink i topbaren, når du scroller helt op.

- Når siden ramte toppen, skiftede Jellyfin 12 topbarens udseende og fjernede samtidig den markering, der gør den gennemsigtig over banneret. I et splitsekund kom temaets farvede bar frem og forsvandt igen. Markeringen sidder nu et sted, Jellyfin ikke rører, så topbaren forbliver gennemsigtig.
- Topbaren bliver nu gennemsigtig med det samme i stedet for at tone ud, så temaets farve ikke hænger et øjeblik i toppen, når du hopper helt op.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Mindre prikker på mobil og tablet.

- Prikkerne, der viser hvilket slide du er på, fyldte omkring halvdelen af skærmbredden på en telefon. De er nu mindre og tættere.
- Den aktive prik blev tegnet i hele sit trykfelt og var derfor en stor hvid plet. Den er nu kun lidt større end de andre.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Ingen streg under den gennemsigtige topbar.

- Skyggen, der holder topbarens knapper læsbare over banneret, sad på selve topbaren og stoppede ved dens underkant, så den tegnede omridset af den gamle topbar. Den ligger nu på banneret og toner blødt ud et godt stykke længere nede.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Gennemsigtig topbar over banneret på Jellyfin 12.

- Banneret går helt op under topbaren, og topbaren er gennemsigtig, så billedet fylder hele toppen af forsiden.
- Når du scroller forbi banneret, bliver topbaren almindelig igen.
- På Favoritter, Tilføj, Kalender og alle andre sider er topbaren som før.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Forsiden indlæses hurtigere.

- Banneret husker sine slides mellem besøg - de skifter alligevel kun hver 48. time - så det vises med det samme, når du åbner appen. Før blev 400 titler hentet igen ved hvert besøg, mens Jellyfins egne rækker ventede.
- Når der skal vælges nye slides, hentes kun id'erne på de 400 kandidater og derefter de 8 valgte, i stedet for alle detaljer om alle 400.
- Afspil/Fortsæt og favorit-hjertet opdateres, når Jellyfins egne rækker er indlæst, så banneret ikke sinker dem.
- Scriptet caches af browseren og hentes kun igen, når plugin'et er opdateret.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Indstillingssiden er tegnet om, så den ser ud som resten af Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin 12 har lavet sine egne indstillingssider om: felterne er nu fyldte bokse med en lille etiket øverst i selve feltet, i stedet for en label ovenover. Denne side fulgte stadig den gamle stil og stak derfor ud fra alt andet i dashboardet.

Felter, afkrydsningsfelter, overskrifter og Gem-knappen matcher nu Jellyfin 12's egne — samme højde, samme afrunding, samme farver. Farverne hentes fra Jellyfin 12's eget tema, så siden også følger med hvis du skifter tema.

Kun udseende. Der er ikke ændret noget i hvad siden gør, eller i indstillingerne selv. På Jellyfin 10.11 ser siden ud præcis som før — den nye stil slås kun til, hvis serveren rent faktisk er 12.

Retter at pluginets indstillingsside ikke kunne åbnes på Jellyfin 12.

Pluginet kørte fint, men dets side under Dashboard → Plugins var der ikke, og der stod ingen fejl nogen steder. Jellyfin 12's nye dashboard viser kun en plugin-indstillingsside, hvis siden selv beder om at komme i menuen. Det gør den nu.

Kun relevant for Jellyfin 12 — på 10.11 kunne siden altid åbnes fra plugin-oversigten uanset hvad.

Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12. Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan KUN installeres der - Jellyfin 10.11 bliver på 2.0.4.0, som stadig virker uændret. Serveren vælger selv den rigtige.

Hvad der skulle laves om: Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende adgangsnøglen på (X-Emby-Token), så alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt i stedet. Uden det svarede serveren 401, og heroens "mest sete"-data kunne ikke hentes.

Accentfarven læses nu direkte fra temaet. Før blev den gættet ved at male en usynlig knap med Jellyfins egne klasser og aflæse farven - men Jellyfin 12 tegner sine knapper på en helt ny måde, hvor den klasse ikke findes, så gættet slog fejl og faldt tilbage til en fast farve. Jellyfin 12 udstiller hele sin farvepalet direkte, så nu bliver den bare spurgt. På 10.11 fungerer den gamle metode som før.

# 🔥 The Biggest Home Screen Sections Update Yet This is the biggest Home Screen Sections update to date, bringing a substantial set of new features, fixes, localisation improvements, and internal changes alongside support for Jellyfin 12. With this release, Home Screen Sections is moving to **3.0.0.0**, marking a major step forward for the plugin and laying the groundwork for future Jellyfin versions. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12**, including updated dependencies and compatibility changes required by the new Jellyfin version. * Added a new **Collections** section to display collections from the user's library. * Added a new **Recently Added In Library** section, allowing recently added media to be displayed for individual libraries, including custom libraries such as Anime (#231). * Added routing to supported sections, allowing section headers such as Genre to link through to their relevant Jellyfin pages. * Added per-section settings, allowing individual sections to have their own configurable behaviour. * Improved **Because You Watched** recommendations with a scoring system to better prioritise similar titles. * Added an option for **Recently Added Shows** to display either shows or individual episodes (#38). * Added an option to filter Upcoming sections based on the user's Jellyfin library access (#214, PR #249, @n00bcodr). * Added warnings when required plugin dependencies cannot be found (#234). * Added separate admin display names for sections, allowing their names to be translated without affecting the title displayed on the home screen. * Integrated with the new **Plugin Pages PluginInterface**, allowing Home Screen Sections to manage its Plugin Pages integration programmatically. ## 🛠️ Improvements * The **Modular Home** menu entry is now registered dynamically through Plugin Pages rather than relying on static Plugin Pages configuration. * The Modular Home page can now be added and removed as part of Home Screen Sections' own lifecycle, reducing the chance of stale or missing Plugin Pages entries. * Improved the reliability of the **Modular Home** link and its integration with Jellyfin's user-facing plugin settings flow. Previous releases have seen cases where the link was missing or resulted in a `Page not found` page. * Home Screen Sections now respects libraries a user has chosen to hide from their home screen, filtering them from relevant sections (PR #237, @gemcdaniel). * Improved compatibility with newer Jellyfin versions by updating library handling and dependency integration. * Improved library filtering to account for changes to `VirtualFolderInfo` in Jellyfin 12. * Improved recommendation behaviour and section configuration through the new per-section settings system. * Improved support for mixed-content and custom libraries across more section types. * Improved Home Screen Sections' handling of temporary user caches, including validation, expiry and automatic cleanup. * Added additional localisation keys throughout the configuration interface to make more of the plugin translatable. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed #269 where cached lazy-load pages could be accessed using a hash created for another user. Added validation, automatic cache cleanup and expiry handling for temporary user caches. * Fixed #268 where the image cache directory wasn't recreated if it was removed while Jellyfin was running. * Fixed #258 by requiring authorization for the section registration endpoint. * Fixed #247 where `/HomeScreen/Sections` could crash when Modular Home was enabled without any globally configured sections. * Fixed #242 where the scroll listener could leak and gradually cause the browser to slow down during long sessions. * Fixed #240 where duplicated file transformations could cause sections to appear multiple times and make configured upper limits, such as Because You Watched's Upper Limit, appear to be ignored. * Fixed #241 where mixed-content libraries weren't supported by the majority of sections. * Fixed #149 where Watch Again, Because You Watched and Genre could fail to return TV series or episodes because queries filtered on parameters which weren't always populated. * Fixed #226 where the Genre section didn't respect the Hide Watched setting (PR #227, @jrhigueras). * Fixed **My Requests** returning unrelated library items when a user had no requested items (PR #246, @jamesmhoward1357). * Fixed library filtering on Jellyfin 12 where `VirtualFolderInfo.ItemId` is no longer populated. * Fixed SkiaSharp dependency compatibility with the newer Jellyfin/.NET stack. * Fixed the Genre section appearing as `{0} Movies` in the admin interface. ## 🌐 Translations * Added **Norwegian Bokmål** translations (PR #239, @dyviknilsen). * Expanded and updated **Polish** translations (PR #235, @TheMatrixan). A large number of new settings, sections and localisation keys have been added in this release. As a result, **some supported languages may not yet have translations for every new string** and may temporarily fall back to English in parts of the plugin. Translation contributions are very welcome! ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The public Home Screen Sections section-registration interface remains compatible with previous releases. * `PluginInterface.RegisterSection(JObject)` is unchanged. * Existing plugins registering custom Home Screen Sections do not need to adopt a new registration payload for this release. * Home Screen Sections itself now consumes the new **Plugin Pages PluginInterface** to register its user-facing Modular Home page dynamically. * Plugins integrating with both Home Screen Sections and Plugin Pages should prefer the new programmatic Plugin Pages API rather than directly modifying Plugin Pages configuration. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12**. * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier Home Screen Sections release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Updated dependencies and internal APIs to align with newer Jellyfin versions. * Home Screen Sections requires compatible releases of **File Transformation** and **Plugin Pages**. * The public Home Screen Sections `PluginInterface.RegisterSection` contract remains compatible with previous releases. ## Contributors * n00bcodr * jrhigueras * jamesmhoward1357 * gemcdaniel * dyviknilsen * TheMatrixan ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

versions.changelog:
### Added

- A Quality column that names the class a frame falls in, from 144p to 8K, with an i in place of the p for interlaced video. It sorts by class rather than by how the name reads, and a filter picks a class from a list and holds rows at, above or below it. (#7)
- `Schema` answers the classes a quality can be held against, in their order.
- A failed export and a failed column save are reported in words of their own.

### Changed

- A CSV names the unit of a size, a runtime and a bitrate in its header. An ODS shows a runtime as a time, counted in hours past a day, and a size and a bitrate with their unit, all of them still numbers a spreadsheet can total. (#6)
- A number typed into a filter with the digit grouping the table prints is read as one number, so 48,000 is no longer 48.
- The README describes `search` and what an export holds, and names bytes per hour and truth values among the filter values.
- An advisory against a package Jellyfin brings along is a build warning rather than an error.

### Fixed

- The sidebar entry followed a language further down the browser's list when English came first, and could take one the browser had ruled out.
- A book ran for the second Jellyfin measures its reading progress in, and was given a size per hour from it.
- A series whose episodes run at 24000/1001 and at 2997/125 read as mixed in its frame rate, though every episode shows 23.976.
- A DVD or Blu-ray folder weighed only the first file of its title. It now weighs every file in the folder and shows no size per hour.
- A .strm took its bitrate and its size per hour from the bytes of the text file.
- The table kept its scroll position when a page turn, a sort, a search or a filter replaced its rows.
- A visit whose schema failed to load left an empty page behind, and a later one left the filter button disabled.
- Two quick changes to the rows per page or to the level a tab is expanded to could be stored in the wrong order.
- The spacing of the tab counts, the column picker and the row toggles did not follow a right-to-left layout.
- Three checks could not fail or skipped part of what they name: the rounded runtime of a series, the version in the README badge, and the names of the tabs.
- A failed library refresh ended the test run, a request the server never answered held it for good, and Ctrl-C waited for the helper container to finish.
- The fixture recipe of the screenshot script went on after a failed encode, and the version list did not retry a connection that dropped after the request was sent.

### Dependencies

- jsdom 30.1.1 in the tests. (#4)
- Renovate keeps `test/` in its scan through an empty `ignorePaths` rather than `ignorePresets`.

### Added

- Conditions on any column, up to twenty per request: at least, at most, equals, differs from, contains, does not contain, is empty and is not empty, whichever of them fit the column. A value is typed in the unit the table shows, a filtered tab lists the level it is expanded to, flat, and an export writes exactly those rows.
- Inventory has its own entry in the dashboard sidebar, worded in the language the browser asks in.
- The table opens on the Inventory logo, worded in the language the page is in and linking to the project.
- Music filed loose beside the albums is listed with them, since no row opens to reach it.
- The plugin archive carries its image, so the catalog and the plugins page show the logo rather than an empty tile.
- `Schema` answers the conditions each column can be held against and how many of them one request may carry.

### Changed

- The Music tab counts tracks rather than albums, and is called Music rather than Albums.
- The table fills the window, with its header held in place while the rows scroll.
- Plays and Plays (all users) read 0 rather than an empty cell, so a condition and a sort can hold them.
- Size, duration and bitrate are held against a range rather than an exact value, which a column shown rounded to a unit could never meet.
- A number is typed with a decimal comma where the language uses one, and a value that cannot be read is marked rather than quietly dropped.
- Leaving the page and coming back finds the tab the way it was left, with its sort and its page.
- Every text cell of a CSV is quoted once it holds a separator, whichever one the file itself uses.
- A film or episode kept in several cuts, any of them split into parts, reports the bytes of every file. It and the folders above it show no size per hour, and its bitrate is that of the cut being served.
- A manual install is described by the plugins folder of the server's data directory, rather than by the Docker path alone.
- Bug reports ask for the steps, a screenshot and the log lines; a pull request agrees to the contributor license agreement by checkbox, which a workflow checks.

### Fixed

- A filtered table of fewer than five rows collapsed to nothing on a low window.
- A film grouped with a version in another library was weighed twice on Jellyfin 12.1.
- A film played in its second cut showed no play count and no date, though Jellyfin counts it played.
- Firefox showed rows above the table header after a wheel scroll.
- A second address for the page bound its controls to the view the web client had kept, leaving the new one empty.
- A page turned inside the pause after typing a condition left the table behind the end of what it lists.
- A page left behind by a library that shrank falls back to the last page there is.
- A condition on a column a plugin update no longer offers took the whole page down, on that visit and every later one.
- The page stops offering conditions once the server would refuse another.
- Exports in Arabic and Persian wrote a decimal separator no spreadsheet reads.
- A download the browser gave up on is no longer logged as a server error.
- A failed request no longer leaves another tab's rows on screen or skips the page, sort and total that are drawn, and the column picker no longer stores a selection for a level that is not shown.
- An expanded row closes again when the table it was opened in is replaced, and expansion requests left over from another tab are no longer sent.
- A numeric first column is no longer right-aligned where rows expand, which hid their indentation, and height is printed without digit grouping.
- The API rejects `parentIds` as soon as one id is not a guid.
- The first build of a table asks which library a folder belongs to once rather than once per item in it.

### Security

- A name holding a semicolon or a tab could start a formula in a spreadsheet set to split there, since only the separator of the file itself was quoted.
- An invented culture name on an export answered with an error and grew a cache that is never freed, and a lone surrogate in a condition answered with an error as well. Both are refused now.
- A configuration saved through Jellyfin's own endpoint with empty lists made every endpoint of the plugin fail until the next restart.

### Dependencies

- Renovate follows the Node, jsdom and Playwright versions the tests are pinned to, alongside the GitHub Actions and the analyzers it already tracked.

### Added

- Rows per page, chosen in the footer and kept across restarts, from 50 up to 10000.
- Three columns totalling playback over every account on the server: how often something was played, when it last was, and how many accounts have played it to the end, which on a folder counts only the accounts that have played everything below it.
- The tab whose rows are on their way and the export being built now show that they are working.
- `Schema` reports the culture it answered in, which is what the page takes its plural form from.

### Changed

- What was labelled Played is now Fully played, since Jellyfin only ticks it when something ran to the end.
- The export is written to a temporary file rather than built in memory, and stops when the browser goes away.
- `Items` and `Export` refuse a sort column they do not know instead of quietly sorting by the first one.
- Every change is tested against each Jellyfin release from 12.0 on, one run per major and minor version, taken from the published image tags.

### Fixed

- A film split across several files reported the size of the first file alone, and no runtime at all.
- A trailer or a making of sitting beside a film was listed as an item of its own, in a tab of its own, and its bytes counted towards the totals.
- The frame rate could read 1000 fps where Jellyfin's own interface shows the real one.
- An item Jellyfin marks played on reaching the end of playback did not reach the table until the next stop report.
- The two dropdowns had no arrow, the search field put an empty label into the toolbar, and a disabled button looked exactly like one that could be clicked.
- A first load that failed left the page blank, with an empty column picker behind the Columns button.
- Expanding a level asked for every fifty rows at once, so a large page could open hundreds of requests at a time.
- A row that turned out to have nothing below it lost its control, its alignment with the rows around it, and the keyboard focus.
- A long path was never shortened, and the footer could not wrap in a narrow window.
- The page indicator is announced when it changes, and the control that opens a row says which row it opens.

### Dependencies

- The release archive is uploaded with the gh CLI; softprops/action-gh-release is no longer used.

### Added

- One table in the dashboard listing everything in the libraries, from a whole series down to a single episode, with 38 columns across General, Video, Audio, Subtitles and Playback.
- Folder rows total what is below them: size, runtime and item count add up, an attribute the children disagree on reads as Mixed, and playback folds from the episodes or tracks underneath.
- A column selection per level and how far a tab opens, both remembered across restarts.
- Search across every level of a tab, sorting on any column, and paging.
- Export of the current view as CSV or ODS, in the language of the interface.
- English, German, Spanish, French and Italian.

JellyToneDown.description: Jellyfin plays a theme song in the background when you open a series or a movie, and offers no way to turn it down. JellyToneDown adds one. A server-wide default plus optional per-user levels, applied to theme songs and the audio of theme videos and to nothing else. The adjustment is made on the server, so it reaches every client - the web player, Swiftfin, Findroid, the Android TV app, Kodi and Infuse alike - rather than only the ones that happen to expose a volume control. Files in your library are never modified; adjusted copies live in Jellyfin's cache. The plugin does not download, assign, rename or otherwise manage theme music. It only changes how loud it is.
JellyToneDown.overview: Adjust the volume of theme music. Just that.

versions.changelog:
- The in-browser slider is now labelled **All themes**, and carries a tooltip saying it applies
  to every title and to your account only. It always worked that way; appearing over a
  particular series just made it look like a per-series control.
- The per-user settings page says the same thing in the same words.
- The slider now stays up for as long as a theme is actually playing, instead of fading after a
  few seconds. Previously, once it had gone there was no way to get it back for the theme
  already playing short of opening a different title. It still fades a few seconds after the
  theme stops, and hovering it keeps it up as before.
- On narrow screens the panel now drops the percentage rather than the "All themes" label, so
  the thing that says what the slider controls survives on a phone.

- The in-browser volume slider no longer needs a writable web client. The script tag is now
  added to `index.html` as the page is served, by middleware, instead of being written into
  the file on disk. That was the one part of the plugin that did not work on a normal package
  install, where the web client is owned by root and Jellyfin runs as its own user - and it
  also means a Jellyfin upgrade can no longer undo it.
- The old on-disk patch is still selectable under **Web client -> How the script gets in**, and
  switching away from it removes anything it previously wrote.
- The config page now reports how many page loads the script has actually been added to, rather
  than only whether it is switched on.
- The catalogue icon is no longer a square that Jellyfin blew up to fill the card.

- Fixed the per-user settings page always reporting an expired session. Jellyfin 12 ships a
  migration that disables legacy authorization, which switches off the `X-Emby-Token` header
  the page was authenticating with. It now uses the standard `Authorization: MediaBrowser`
  scheme.
- Added a plugin icon.
- Per-version release notes: every version used to read "Initial release" in the catalogue.

- Added a per-user settings page at `/JellyToneDown/MySettings`, so users can set their own
  theme volume without dashboard access. (Shipped broken - fixed in 1.0.2.)
- Adjusted copies are now encoded at the lower of the source bitrate and a per-codec ceiling
  rather than always around 190 kbps, so a 128 kbps theme is no longer inflated.
- The encoder settings are part of the cache key, so changing them invalidates the cache by
  itself.
- Fixed the config page status panel printing the same sentence twice.
- Initial release.

JellyTrend.description: Syncs TMDB trending movies & TV shows with your local library and provides a Netflix-style banner carousel on the home screen.
JellyTrend.overview: JellyTrend empareja contenido en tendencia de TMDB con tu biblioteca Jellyfin usando provider IDs, genera recomendaciones personalizadas por usuario y lo muestra en un carrusel de banners y en canales para todos los clientes.

versions.changelog:
Novedades en 3.0.1

Reproducción
- Android TV: los ítems de los canales vuelven a reproducirse. El plugin deja que Jellyfin asigne el id correcto a las fuentes; antes Android TV devolvía un id que no coincidía y la petición acababa en NoCompatibleStream.
- El canal de Recomendados refresca su caché al reproducir un título, sin esperar a la siguiente rotación.

Sin duplicados
- Las sombras de los canales se marcan como virtuales y se desvinculan de personas, géneros, estudios, tags y provider ids.
- Ya no aparecen en la búsqueda, páginas de actores/géneros/estudios, sugerencias, Últimas añadidas ni Continuar viendo. El detalle del canal conserva título, sinopsis, nota, duración e imágenes.
- La limpieza es automática en cada sincronización, al arrancar y cada 15 minutos.

Carrusel
- Inyección en memoria: ya no se modifica jellyfin-web/index.html. Funciona con Jellyfin como servicio de Windows (Servicio de red) y sin permisos de escritura sobre Program Files.
- Carga dirigida por eventos, solo en Inicio, sin peticiones anónimas y con URLs de imagen escaladas por Jellyfin.
- Si el carrusel está desactivado, el endpoint no devuelve datos aunque el navegador tenga el script cacheado.

Almacenamiento y recomendaciones
- PostgreSQL es el almacén autoritativo cuando el proveedor está activo; la copia JSON es opcional y viene desactivada.
- Migraciones automáticas al esquema privado (versión 5).
- Afinidades con normalización global, personas recurrentes, puntuaciones persistidas y exclusión estricta de títulos vistos o en curso.

Compatibilidad
- Jellyfin 12.1.x con .NET 10 (targetAbi 12.1.0.0). Para Jellyfin 10.11.x usa la versión 2.0.4.
- Tras actualizar, ejecuta una vez las tareas de sincronización o reinicia para normalizar las sombras existentes.

Validación: build Release sin advertencias; 95/95 pruebas correctas.

3.0.0 - El plugin pasa a aprender el gusto de cada usuario

Refactor casi completo desde la 2.0.4: la lista de tendencias de TMDB deja de ser el centro y el perfil de cada usuario pasa a serlo. Requiere .NET 10.

Novedades
- Motor de recomendaciones por usuario: afinidades (generos, decadas, personas, valoraciones, duracion) aprendidas del consumo real, y puntuacion de cada titulo de la biblioteca contra ese perfil.
- Arranque en frio: mientras un usuario no alcanza el minimo de titulos vistos (configurable), su fila se arma con lo que ve el resto del servidor.
- Reserva y rotacion: la lista guardada es mas larga que la fila visible y va cambiando de punto de partida cada cierto tiempo.
- Reparto series/peliculas en la lista de Trendings, con relleno para que la fila nunca quede corta.
- Items de canal materializados para todos los usuarios (ya no dependen de que alguien abra el canal) y cache por usuario en los dos canales, sin fugas entre usuarios.
- El perfil se refresca con los eventos de reproduccion, sin esperar a la corrida programada.
- Panel nuevo de cuatro pestanas (Trendings, Recomendaciones, Almacenamiento y Actividad), con icono propio en la barra lateral, textos en espanol e ingles, estado real del almacenamiento e historial de cada corrida.
- Almacen opcional en PostgreSQL: con el PostgreSQL Database Provider los datos viven en el esquema jellytrend con historial, y las recomendaciones pasan a SQL nativo optimizado (4-10x). Los JSON de la carpeta de datos quedan como copia de cortesia.
- README en espanol (por defecto) y en ingles, con capturas de las cuatro pestanas, el carrusel y los dos canales.

Compatibilidad
- Jellyfin 12.1.x - .NET 10.
- Para Jellyfin 10.11.x usa la version 2.0.4.
