versions.changelog:
## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## User
- The Refresh Guide progress is now more accurate

## User
- Channels now direct play on clients that support the stream instead of always being remuxed or transcoded by the server

## Developer
- The opened source now sets SupportsDirectPlay. PlaybackInfo always disables direct stream (MediaInfoHelper), so a source that only allowed direct stream could never be picked and every tune-in fell back to DirectPlayError and a remux

## User
- A channel with no viewers now stops when its countdown reaches zero. It used to run on for two to three minutes after the last viewer left
- Tune-in cards are generated for every channel shortly after the server starts and at every guide refresh, including the refresh a save triggers, so a fresh install, an update, a new logo, or changed output settings never leave a channel opening without its card

## Developer
- The linger teardown was vetoed every time because the Jellyfin reader is served right up to the close, so the two-minute recent-delivery rule always saw a viewer at the 30s mark, and the one-shot task then gave up until the reaper backstop 90s plus a minute later. A lingering session now only counts delivery after the close (DeliveryCountsAsWatched, unit tested), and LingerTeardownAsync retries every 5s until the reaper threshold
- LiveChannelsTvService sweeps the tune-in cards 20s after construction and from every GetChannelsAsync (EnsureLogoAsync then IntroService.EnsureAsync per enabled channel, serialised, logged with its trigger); a tune-in without a card now logs it
- The Sessions tab countdown wording no longer uses an em dash or a semicolon

## User
- Tune-in is now immediate. A channel opens on a short animated card (its logo and a Starting Channel caption over flowing lines) the moment you tune in, while the content is seeked and encoded behind it, and the picture no longer waits ten seconds or more for a buffer to fill first
- The Start-up buffer setting is gone. It turned out to be a literal pause Jellyfin applied before every tune-in rather than a buffer, and the cushion it was meant to provide is now built up while you are already watching

## Developer
- Removed StartupBufferSeconds and BufferMs (Jellyfin sleeps for BufferMs in TranscodeManager.AcquireResources before launching the delivery ffmpeg, on every tune-in including adoption)
- The tune-in handover now waits for the playlist and one segment instead of the full cushion, and the endpoint reader's hold-back ramps in one segment per ten seconds of session age instead of applying from the first byte
- Segments and the encoder GOP are now three seconds, matching Jellyfin's delivery remux so every stage cuts on the same keyframes

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a live_tv icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

- Administrators can now copy central groups into their own personal collection when switching back to personal mode, or import them later. Both management screens require an explicit copy/skip choice on mode switch. Existing personal groups take precedence when IDs match; central groups and other users' personal groups remain untouched. Custom group images are copied with newly imported groups.
- Require administrators to explicitly choose whether to copy their personal groups when switching to central management. The no-copy choice preserves personal groups for later use, and both the web dialog and plugin dashboard offer a later import. Reject an ambiguous mode-switch request instead of silently showing an empty central group list.

- Support Wholphin in the native Live TV guide: select a group or **All channels** directly in its compatible Control Center folders, then open **Live TV → TV Guide**. Group selection applies only to the authenticated user's device, respects current group/channel permissions, and restores the full guide on reset. Wholphin does not support an automatic guide jump.
- Add administrator switches for the official Jellyfin Android TV / Fire TV app and Wholphin. A sole eligible TV is selected automatically; with several TVs, the last available choice is remembered per user. Disabled or disconnected devices cannot receive playback or guide changes.
- Add recognizable artwork to the Control Center home tile, guide actions, confirmation and fallback folders. **All channels** has its own EPG-reset image; created groups have a distinct group image. Personal and shared groups can use custom PNG, JPEG or WebP images up to 5 MiB, with preview and reset controls and permission checks.
- Add recording controls to the grouped web EPG. Users with Jellyfin's Live TV management permission can schedule, edit and cancel single-program or series timers, including padding and series options; recording errors remain visible in the dialog.
- Restore reliable loading of the independent web EPG behind reverse proxies that cached its old script URL. Preserve original channel logos, official Android TV / Fire TV behavior, channel playback and the existing plugin identity and settings.

- Selecting a group in the official Android TV / Fire TV app immediately applies that group's native guide scope and opens the ordinary Live TV view. The separate Native TV guide action remains available to retry.
- Hide direct grouped-channel media tiles from that authenticated TV response while keeping the native guide action and browsable program-list fallback. Internal channel items and playlists remain unchanged.
- Retain per-user/device validation, group access checks and safe behavior when navigation is unavailable. The original app may still require selecting TV Guide after opening Live TV; a direct timeline deep link is not exposed by the stock client.

- Organize Live TV channels in ordered personal groups independent of IPTV-provider categories, or use administrator-managed shared groups with per-group user access.
- Show one selected group's original channels in Jellyfin's native Android TV / Fire TV timeline. Select the group on the TV or from the web/mobile page; the web page can also apply the deduplicated union of all visible groups. Reset to all ordinarily permitted channels at any time. versions.changelog:
- Initial release. - Resolution (isHd/is4K) passthrough for client filtering. - Fix: filtering by a library returned no items. The library (parentId) is now
  resolved into its contents so video range / codec / audio filters work when
  scoped to a specific library.
- Renamed the plugin to "Marquee Companion" (display name only; API route,
  plugin id, and behavior unchanged).
- Capabilities are now scoped to the requested library (parentId): the available
  values offered for a library are drawn only from items in that library, so any
  single facet selection is guaranteed to match at least one item there. Omitting
  parentId still returns the global value set.
- TV libraries now filter correctly by stream facets. Stream attributes live on
  episodes, but TV libraries are browsed at the series level; the filter now
  matches episodes and returns the shows that have at least one matching episode.
  Also forces a recursive query so a library id resolves to its contents.
- Added opt-in recent podcast discovery through Podcast Index. - Podcast discovery now logs why it returned nothing. The endpoint still answers 404 for
  every failure, but the server log distinguishes disabled credentials, a Podcast Index
  rejection, and feeds dropped during validation — including a per-rule tally of what was
  dropped.
- Removes the YouTube trailer resolver. Clients now hand YouTube trailers to the YouTube
  app instead, so the server no longer downloads, verifies, updates, or executes yt-dlp or a
  JavaScript runtime.
- Removes the yt-dlp and JavaScript-runtime downloads earlier versions installed. Those
  binaries are unreachable now the resolver is gone, so the plugin reclaims the directory it
  created rather than leaving an administrator to find it. Only its own install root is
  touched, and a failure to delete never stops the plugin starting.
- Fix: Podcast Discovery always returned 404 when enabled. Podcast Index sends the envelope's
  `status` as a JSON boolean, but it was bound to a string, so the whole recent-feeds payload
  failed to deserialize. Both the boolean and the documented string form are now accepted, and
  an unusable payload is logged with the value exactly as it arrived.
- Added opt-in email sign-in. A client posts an email address, the server mails a single-use
  link, and confirming that link signs the waiting device in — no password, and no typing on a
  TV remote. The email can be opened on any device, so it works for tvOS; when it is opened on
  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into
  the app. Unrecognised addresses can optionally register, in which case the new account is
  created disabled and copies an administrator-chosen template user's permissions, so nothing is
  accessible until an administrator enables it. SMTP host, port, security, credentials and
  from-address are configured in the plugin settings, along with link lifetime and rate limits;
  a "send test email" button reports the mail server's own error when submission fails. The
  endpoint reports an explicit error rather than a silent success when SMTP is not configured.
- Fix: an audio filter matched files that had each thing you asked for, but never in
  the same track. Asking for AC-3 in 5.1 returned 444 movies on a test library, of which
  only 247 had an AC-3 track that was itself 5.1 — the rest were "DTS 5.1 main track plus
  AC-3 2.0 commentary" files that answered "has AC-3" and "has six channels" separately.
  Codec, channel count and spatial format are now read per audio track and have to hold on
  ONE of them. A filter naming a single audio facet is unaffected. The values offered by
  /Capabilities are unchanged.
- Music libraries can now be filtered by codec and channel count. Tracks were never

# 🎬 Media Bar Arrives on Jellyfin 12

Media Bar **3.0.0.0** brings support for **Jellyfin 12**, including compatibility with both the classic desktop experience and Jellyfin's newer modern web layout.

> ## 🙌 Huge thanks to MakD and the upstream contributors
>
> Media Bar itself is the work of **MakD and the contributors to the upstream Media Bar project**. The plugin I maintain is primarily a Jellyfin wrapper around that work, exposing configuration and integration points so it can be installed and managed cleanly as a Jellyfin plugin.
>
> A huge amount of effort has gone into keeping Media Bar working across Jellyfin's changing web interface, especially for Jellyfin 12. The features, UI work and frontend improvements in this release are built on that upstream work, and the credit for that belongs to **MakD and everyone contributing there**.
>
> My part is largely packaging, integrating and exposing that work through Jellyfin's plugin system.

## ✨ New Features

* Added support for **Jellyfin 12**.
* Added support for Jellyfin 12's **modern React/MUI home screen layout**, alongside the existing classic desktop layout.
* Updated the bundled Media Bar frontend to the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream version.
* Added Jellyfin 12-specific styling so Media Bar integrates correctly with the new web-client shell while retaining the existing appearance on the classic layout.
* Media Bar continues to ship its frontend assets directly with the plugin, ensuring the version displayed in Jellyfin matches the plugin version you've installed.

## 🛠️ Improvements

* Synced Media Bar with the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream work.
* Improved Media Bar placement within the Jellyfin 12 home screen across both supported layouts.
* Improved layout behaviour on taller displays, ensuring Jellyfin's home-screen rows remain below the Media Bar content rather than overlapping its controls.
* Improved localisation handling when loading Jellyfin's translation chunks.
* Retained support for the **Get updates early** option for users who explicitly want to track unreleased upstream Media Bar changes.

## 🪲 Bug Fixes

* Fixed Media Bar being inserted in the wrong position when using Jellyfin 12's modern layout (#181).
* Fixed translated Media Bar strings falling back to English or producing JSON decoding errors for some languages (#185).
* Fixed home-screen rows overlapping Media Bar buttons on taller viewports.
* Fixed Jellyfin 12 layout differences that could cause Media Bar to render incorrectly compared with Jellyfin 10.11.

## ⚠️ Compatibility

* **Media Bar 3.0.0.0 supports Jellyfin 10.11.11 and Jellyfin 12.**
* Users on older Jellyfin 10.x versions should remain on a compatible **2.x** Media Bar release.
* Jellyfin 12 support includes both the **classic Desktop layout** and the newer **modern React/MUI layout**.
* A compatible **File Transformation 3.x** release is required.
* If you're using the **Get updates early** option, unreleased upstream Media Bar changes may behave differently from the frontend bundled and tested with this plugin release.

## Contributors

* austinnorgaard
* judarange

## ❤️ Support

If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27).

Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

Hotfix for 1.0.8.0 — the Issues tab went blank and unresponsive on servers with substantial history.

Root cause: the new per-row "last attempt" lookup in 1.0.8.0 ran a correlated subquery against the history table with no supporting index. On loaded databases the query stalled long enough that Jellyfin tore down the request scope mid-flight, which crashed MVC's result serializer with ObjectDisposedException — the Issues tab silently rendered empty and every button that depended on live issue data felt dead.

Schema v11 adds a covering index on history(issue_id, dry_run, fixed_at_utc). Non-destructive migration: SQLite builds the index from existing rows. No rescan, no history loss, no re-queue needed.

Measured ~450x speed-up on the correlated query (approx 5000ms -> approx 15ms per 500-id chunk on a 48k-row history), and GET /MediaDash/Issues?openOnly=true now returns a steady HTTP 200 instead of timing out and 500ing. 1526 / 1526 tests green.

Fixes #80.

Protection: right-click (or long-press) in the Files tab to protect any file/folder from scans and fixes, or push one into the issue queue.

"Original language" option added to audio/subtitle pickers. (#78)

Format converters for images, music and video (RMVB → MKV), with a first-run wizard step to enable them.

SMART monitoring is disable-able per server via right-click on the SMART pill. (#60)

Per-fixer disable toggle in Settings → Fix order.

Playability: catches damaged secondary audio tracks; books and comics refused with a doc-aware message; audio files with cover art no longer false-flagged. (#75, #76)

Repair + conversion safety: source identity captured before encoding, output verified against source duration/stream count, audiobook merges won't overwrite an existing .m4b. Alternate audio tracks preserved on RMVB → MKV remuxes.

Scanning: Photos library now covered; Overview breakdown includes Music/Books/Photos; `.txt` books aren't flagged as orphans; respects Enabled Libraries setting.

Cross-volume moves refuse symlinks/junctions and verify inventory before deleting the source.

Many UI fixes across Issues tab, Settings, Overview and Recycle. "Reset scan data" preserves Queued/Dismissed decisions.

Light-mode: Files-tab right-click menu and Protect dialog are now readable under the Light theme.

Calibre: no longer hangs on verbose installers; paths with spaces work; override path changes picked up without restart.

Hotfix for 1.0.7.6 Playability false-positives.

• Removed the bitrate-vs-size pre-filter that flagged efficient x264 rips (YIFY / small MP4 rips of Severance / Landman / Rage / Outlander at 400 MB–2.4 GB) as size-truncated. Decode-check already catches genuine tail-truncation with far fewer false positives.

1.0.7.4 is a small follow-up to 1.0.7.3's combined audio + subtitle cleanup pass, closing the last case where MediaDash could ffmpeg the same file twice in one fix run.

When a file had a queued re-encode AND queued track cleanup (unwanted audio or subtitle languages), it used to remux for the tracks first and then re-encode a second time. The re-encode already drops unwanted tracks by itself, so the first remux was wasted work — and if it didn't run first, it would fail with "nothing to remove" once the re-encode had finished. Now the fix run detects the overlap and lets the re-encode handle both jobs in one pass. Same recycle bin entry, one history row per issue, both track and quality issues flip to Fixed together.

User-visible impact: multi-language 4K remuxes that also need size reduction finish in half the time, and the Errors tab stops picking up spurious "nothing to remove" failures on files that were just re-encoded.

New Overview banner warns when a MediaDash re-encode gets undone by something external (typically Sonarr/Radarr redownloading a "too-small" file whose size dropped below the quality profile minimum, but also fires on manual recycle-bin restores or backup-restore overwrites).

Detection is evidence-based, not guessed: at the end of every scan MediaDash walks the last 30 days of successful non-dry-run history entries, and for each one where the ORIGINAL is still preserved in the recycle bin, compares the file currently at the same path against the recycled original. If the current file is within 10% of the original size â€” i.e. the same rough size we shrank down â€” the shrunk copy has been replaced. Only paths meeting that concrete size-match trigger the warning. False positives are limited to genuine restores, which are also worth surfacing.

The red banner shows the filename, the shrunk-to size, the current size, and the fix date. Dismissable per browser session; reappears on the next scan if the condition still holds.

Two fixes and a reclaim.

VAAPI hardware encodes now pass -rc_mode VBR to hevc_vaapi / h264_vaapi / av1_vaapi. Mesa VAAPI's default rate-control is CQP, which ignores -b:v/-maxrate and picks a QP that routinely produces output LARGER than a modest-bitrate source â€” the "the re-encoded file would be larger than the original, so the original was kept" retry loop that some AMD iGPU users saw every 30-70 minutes on the same file. VBR honours -b:v as the target and -maxrate as the ceiling, so the encoder actually stays under the requested bitrate.

Orphan sidecar sweep: at the end of every fix run (right after the recycle bin purge), MediaDash now walks each library root and deletes any *.mediadash.tmp*, *.mediadash.new*, mediadash.tmp.*, or mediadash.new.* file it finds. These are leftovers from a hard-killed encode (SIGKILL, container restart, Jellyfin crash) where the C# finally block that normally deletes them never ran. Deleted-count + reclaimed-bytes go into Jellyfin's log.

FfmpegExecutor now sweeps for orphaned MediaDash ffmpeg processes before spawning a new encode. Linux only (reads /proc/<pid>/cmdline; Windows/macOS would need extra deps for a very rare failure mode). Any ffmpeg whose command line contains a mediadash.tmp or mediadash.new marker is killed with SIGKILL and its sidecar output file is deleted. Prevents the "two ffmpegs writing to the same output" scenario after a plugin hot-reload or a Jellyfin restart mid-encode. Also cleans up the interleaved-bytes .tmp file that would otherwise sit on disk until the next fix run on the same source overwrote it.

Manual fix runs now pause instead of bailing when someone starts watching. Click "Run fixes now", the queue drains as before, but if the pause-on-playback check trips between files the run pauses (with an amber banner: "Paused: someone is watching. Click 'Ignore activity' to resume anyway.") and re-checks every 30 seconds. When the viewer stops or you hit the Ignore activity button, the run resumes from where it stopped. Scheduled runs keep the previous behaviour (break on activity, next 15-minute tick tries again). The Ignore flag only applies to the current run â€” a fresh Run fixes now click brings the pause behaviour back.

Fix the "Fix run finished with failures" popup firing on every page load. The first-poll guard checked prevFinishedAt !== undefined but lastStatus starts as null, which short-circuited prevFinishedAt to null (not undefined) â€” so opening the plugin page always fired an alert if the most-recent completed run had any failures, even while a new run was still going. The alert now only fires when a poll's FinishedAtUtc actually changes from a prior poll.

Fix cascade after 0.9.3 hit real prod hardware. Track-remux fixer now uses the same hash-fallback sidecar name as the transcode fixer (v0.9.2 shipped it for one path, not both) â€” long-UTF-8 filenames (Cyrillic/CJK) no longer fail with ffmpeg "Error opening output" on Linux NAME_MAX. Free-disk-space check now looks at the actual mount containing the file via RecycleBin.FindDriveForPath, not the root filesystem â€” LXC/Docker setups where /mnt/media is a large bind-mount but / is a tiny rootfs no longer get false "Not enough free disk space" bailouts on 30-60 GB BDRemuxes. QualityScanner is less trigger-happy: dropped the container-level bitrate fallback (was flagging remuxes with big lossless audio as "video too fat"), and added a 15%-of-file-size minimum-savings gate so HEVC->HEVC recompression at close bitrates doesn't burn a 20-minute encode only for the fixer to abort with "the re-encoded file would be larger than the original". TrackFixer's error truncation matches TranscodeFixer now â€” keeps the ffmpeg-error tail (where the real reason lives), not the head.

Transcode fix now actually uses the GPU. v0.9.2 shipped without the hardware-encoder path wired in â€” the UseHardwareEncoder toggle had no effect and every re-encode ran on the CPU via libx265. This release wires the hw path through and adds full VAAPI support (device auto-picked from /dev/dri/renderD* or Jellyfin's VaapiDevice, with format=nv12,hwupload / scale_vaapi in the filter chain). When Jellyfin's own HardwareAccelerationType is unset, the plugin now autodetects: NVIDIA â†’ NVENC, any Linux DRM device (Intel/AMD iGPU or dGPU) â†’ VAAPI, Windows â†’ AMF (or QSV for Intel iGPUs), macOS â†’ VideoToolbox, and falls back to libx265 only when no GPU is present. Any hardware failure still retries with software so no encode gets stuck. Settings page tidy-up: 'Thorough playability check' no longer has the oversized inset box beside the disposal dropdown; Issues tab drops the redundant 'Show' type filter (the count pills already do that) and moves the filename search onto the same row.

Groups TV episodes into per-show folders and movie franchises (>=2 siblings) into shared folders using Jellyfin's identified metadata. Fixes false-positive duplicate detection when Jellyfin derives Movie.Name from a folder (name-fallback keys now include the filename; also tightened for Book and Audio, with a required runtime for audio). Fixes transcode failure on filenames near Linux's 255-byte limit (Cyrillic/CJK) via hash-based sidecar names. Failed fixes that mean 'file no longer exists' or 'nothing left to remove' now auto-clear from the queue instead of retrying every 15 minutes. Move-style fixers now update sibling issues in the DB so they don't fail with 'no longer exists' after a rename. Issues tab: per-type total pills, 'Try to play' button on Playability cards, Duplicate cards show keeper location. ffmpeg error output now shows the tail (where the actual error is) instead of the codec startup banner.

MediaTools.overview: Media management swiss army knife: zero-interruption renaming, split-movie merging, MKV remuxing and stream deduplication.

Mind the Gaps.description: Scans your library for gaps (missing movies in partially-owned collections and franchises, missing series content, unowned titles from actor and director filmographies, and related recommendations) using TMDB, Trakt, TheTVDB, and TVmaze, with music and book sources (MusicBrainz, OpenLibrary, Discogs), and reads the watchlists and want-lists you already keep on those sites. Presents an easy todo list for filling out your collection, diagnoses why a title is reported missing, surfaces where to watch each item, and can optionally mint native virtual placeholders for missing items.
Mind the Gaps.overview: Find what's missing and related in your library and build a todo list to complete it.

versions.changelog: 10.11.11.0 - Want to watch gains three options, all off by default and all requiring the arrived-titles playlist (contributed by David Rappo, @rappo, in PR 21): the home row can lead with the titles already on your playlist, a title comes off the playlist once it is watched (a series once every episode is played), and a movie or series page gets a bookmark button among its own. Plugin rows are reachable with a TV remote's D-pad. Not interested, off by default, lets each user hide a title from their own Web UI pages without hiding it for anyone else. A user with a parental rating limit sees the Web UI sections narrowed to the titles that limit allows, rather than none of them. The home Discover row, the Want to watch row, and the item page rows each have a placement setting; existing settings carry over. The Gaps Report's toolbar is grouped by what each control acts on, every header has a select-all, a line above the list says how many rows the filters hide, and Add to TODO is now Add to watchlist. The report is usable at phone width, and the settings page has collapsible sections, a search, and better screen reader support. A new scheduled task, Prune gaps from deleted items, takes deleted library items out of the report: a gap they were the only source of is removed, and one with other sources moves to the next. It has no default schedule; it waits for a running scan, and a second scan waits for the first. Recommendation groups link to the owned title they came from. Books get an OpenLibrary id field and albums and artists a Discogs id field in the metadata editor, with a link on the item's page; a dedicated OpenLibrary or Discogs plugin takes over when installed. Links are built from each title's ids when the report loads, so a link plugin installed later applies everywhere. The report takes far less memory and disk (on a library with 83,000 gaps, about 1.6 GB down to 200 MB in memory and 245 MB down to 131 MB on disk), loads in about half the time, and is written far less often during scans and where-to-watch lookups. Existing reports convert on first load; a report saved by this version cannot be read by an earlier one, so going back shows an empty report until its next scan.

10.11.10.0 - The Maintenance section has a Fulfillment queue for an administrator who fetches titles by hand. It folds every user's TODO list into one row per title, sorted by how many people still want it, names who is still waiting, and shows the streaming-service icons as soon as the queue opens, with the same links a TODO row already has. Mark fetched closes the title for every requester in one action, and Verify all checks the queue against the library and closes a title you already have, however it arrived. With Everyone's watchlist on (off by default), that same household list is a Discover source and leads the Discover view of every domain it has entries for. Send to the acquisition stack is done from the Gaps Report. The report's Send action has a quality profile picker, filled from the stack's own profile list and preselecting the profile you configured, so an older title the default profile cannot find a release for can still be sent. The report's My TODO list popup is gone; the Fulfillment queue is where an administrator sees every list. The report's multi-select bar can Acquire, Request, or Resolve a checked batch (Resolve applies one shared note), alongside Mint and Add to TODO. An administrator can manage another user's want-to-watch list. With "Want to watch: move arrived titles into a playlist" on, a title that is in the library moves into that user's own Jellyfin playlist the next time it is verified, so it shows up in every client. The playlist is named Want to Watch unless you change it, and only a real file counts as arrived. Amazon and web-search links for a book or album include the author or artist, on the report, the Web UI, and the Fulfillment queue. TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and OpenLibrary subjects are set with the same chip pickers the other curated sources use. A book's dialog loads its description from OpenLibrary when you open it. Studio pages, off by default, add a Missing from the studio row of that studio's movies you do not own, on the list page you open from a movie's studio credit. A library that sets a metadata fetcher order keeps TVmaze in the series check. TVmaze is not a Jellyfin metadata fetcher, so it is always asked and ranked last.

10.11.9.0 - Mind the Gaps now reaches into Jellyfin's own pages through an experimental, opt-in Web UI, with a master switch and one toggle per surface in settings, all off by default. A person's page lists what they made that you do not own, a movie or series page suggests titles like it that you are missing, an artist's page lists the albums you do not have, and a book page or an author's own page lists more by the same author. The home page can show a Discover row of the recommendations your scans found from titles you own and from lists that are public by nature (TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and TMDB's own feeds), never from a watchlist, wantlist, favorites, or a personal list. Click a card for a detail dialog with TMDB's synopsis, genres, runtime, rating, a trailer link, and a link to the title's JustWatch page, then send it to Radarr or Sonarr with the quality profile you pick; the dialog and the card grids can be driven from a keyboard or a TV remote. A user with a parental rating limit is shown none of these sections. With Want to watch turned on, every card carries a bookmark that adds the title to your own list, and the home page can show a Want to watch row of what you have listed and do not yet own. The TODO list is now kept per user, in the plugin's data folder, and removed when the user is deleted; the first administrator to open the old shared list takes it over, and an administrator can switch the report's TODO to everyone's lists to see and manage them. The Gaps Report loads faster: it fetches one tab at a time as slim rows, fetches a row's details only when you open it, revalidates what it already holds instead of downloading it again, and loads its script and stylesheet as separately cached files; the saved report is stored as one file per domain, and an existing report is converted automatically. A row shows up to two streaming-service icons, following your provider and monetization filters and wearing the service's logo (a service TMDB lists as several providers, such as a "with Ads" tier, shows as one icon and one provider filter entry), and clicking them opens the title's TMDB watch page. Gaps left behind by a source you have since removed or turned off are pruned on every scan, and a Prune stale gaps button under Maintenance does it right away. A TMDB list that cannot be read, such as a private one, no longer stops the other lists from being scanned, filling in a large library's series content is done in batches, and the scan log says how long each source took. New, and off by default: the report and the Web UI can load their posters, covers, and streaming-service logos through your server instead of each browser fetching them from TMDB and the other providers. Turn on "Keep the pages' images on this server" in the new Images section of settings; the server fetches each image once, from a fixed list of provider hosts only, keeps it under its cache folder, and sends the browser on to the provider whenever it cannot serve one, and a "Trim the image cache" scheduled task keeps the cache to the size you set (500 MB by default).

10.11.8.0 - The Gaps Report is reorganized around your library's domains: Movies, Shows, Music, and Books are now the primary tabs, each badged with its own gap count, with Set completion, Creator works, and Discover scoped underneath as a view you pick per domain, so only the active domain's data is loaded at a time. A Compact view toggle switches to a denser layout. Click a title to expand its detail in place: the overview, where to watch, and (outside Compact view) every information and action button tile inline instead of opening separate popovers; collapsed, the same actions live behind three icon popovers on the row, and a collapsed title's own browser tooltip shows its overview with no click at all. The toolbar is split into a filter row and an action row, and the settings page is reorganized into one collapsible section per provider (TMDB, Trakt, MDBList, Discogs, OpenLibrary, TheTVDB, IMDb, JustWatch), each badged on or off, with a search box that opens whichever section matches. Four new TMDB feeds, Top Rated, Popular, Upcoming, and Now Playing, can be turned on individually under Discover, and Jellyfin 12.0 is now a supported target alongside 10.11, each release building and shipping its own ABI-matched package. Gaps now show real cover art for books (bibliography and subject lists), music (MusicBrainz discography and artist works), and series completion episodes (TMDB, TheTVDB, and TVmaze all supply a still where they have one) instead of a blank thumbnail, falling back to the placeholder rather than a broken-image icon when a cover fails to load; MDBList entries carry a poster and description like every other source. A creator's page can be trimmed further with a minimum TMDB vote count for a movie credit and a minimum episode count for a TV credit. The TODO list shows an image and release date per entry. Sending a whole-series gap to Sonarr from a filmography, recommendation, or favorites entry sends the series' own title rather than the name of whatever surfaced it, and a rejected Radarr, Sonarr, or Jellyseerr request shows the service's validation message instead of a raw response body.

versions.changelog:
Burger-menu på brede skærme.

Jellyfin 12 viser kun burger-knappen i smalle vinduer. Denne version lægger en
burger-knap i venstre side af app-baren på brede skærme også. Den åbner den
samme menu - med ekstra-punkterne øverst og Seerr Requests-linksene - og
skjules igen, mens en video spiller.

Slås til under "Burger menu on desktop screens". Ingen effekt på Jellyfin 10.11
eller i smalle vinduer.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Baggrundsbilledet på detaljesider lægger sig ikke længere oven på Jellyfins eget. Jellyfin tegner selv et baggrundsbillede i vinduer over 1000 px, og det kunne nå frem, mens vores stadig blev hentet - så lå der to lag og tonede hen over hinanden. Kontrollen sker nu lige før billedet sættes ind, i stedet for inden hentningen begynder.

Målt på Jellyfin 12: ved 1200 px vinder Jellyfins eget, ved 900 px vores. Begge dele sker, og i begge tilfælde vises nu præcis ét billede.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Baggrundsbilledet på detaljesider hentes nu i vinduets egen bredde i stedet for det dobbelte. På en skærm med skalering bad siden før om et 2560 px bredt billede til et 1268 px vindue; nu er det 1280 px - omkring en fjerdedel så mange bytes, og en størrelse serveren som regel har lavet i forvejen.

Billedet ligger bag et mørkt slør, hvor detaljerne alligevel ikke kan ses. Kort og plakater er uændrede: de ses tæt på og hentes stadig i skærmens egen opløsning.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Den natlige billedopvarmning tager nu kun titler, der er kommet til inden for de sidste 45 dage. Hele biblioteket køres igennem om søndagen, så billedstørrelser, en ny app begynder at bede om, stadig bliver lavet på forhånd.

Målt på serveren: den natlige kørsel så på 69.174 billeder for at lave 7.513 af dem og tog halvanden time, fordi resten allerede var lavet og kun blev tjekket.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Det første kort, du holder musen over efter en sideindlæsning, viser nu også forhåndsvisningen. Rækken kom på skærmen et halvt sekund før den begyndte at lytte efter musen, så den første bevægelse blev tabt - derfor virkede det næste kort med det samme, og det første bagefter.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Forhåndsvisningen på Fortsæt afspilning starter med det samme i stedet for efter tre sekunder, og klikker du på kortet, fortsætter afspilningen dér, hvor forhåndsvisningen er nået til.

I browsere uden forbindelse til serverens fjernbetjening starter klikket stadig - dér fra det gemte sted, et par sekunder før billedet på skærmen.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Et klik på Fortsæt afspilning afspiller med det samme, også i browsere hvor Jellyfins fjernbetjening ikke har forbindelse - dér endte klikket før på afsnittets side.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Forsiden står stille igen på Jellyfin 12.

- Fortsæt afspilning og Næste afsnit er én række igen, og Trending virker igen. Den gav op, når andre havde set mange afsnit den seneste måned.
- Rækkerne hopper ikke længere rundt, mens forsiden indlæses, og billederne på Fortsæt afspilning skifter ikke: de viser seriens billede, ligesom Jellyfins egen række.
- Ingen S/E-mærker på Fortsæt afspilning.
- Filmbibliotekernes redesign (Anbefalet til dig, favoritter og filtre) er fjernet, så bibliotekerne ser ud som i Jellyfin selv.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Hurtigere billeder overalt: forsiden, søgningen og detaljesiderne.

- Jellyfin laver et billede i en ny størrelse første gang, nogen beder om den, og det tager 0,1-0,5 sekunder pr. billede. Apps beder om lidt forskellige størrelser på hver enhed og i hvert vindue, så de fleste billeder blev lavet forfra. Størrelserne rundes nu til en kort liste, så et billede lavet til én enhed genbruges af den næste, og kvalitet over 90 sættes ned til 90 - et plakatkort fylder omkring en tredjedel mindre uden synlig forskel. Gælder alle apps.
- Ny planlagt opgave "Warm image cache" (dagligt kl. 03:00) laver plakater, baggrunde, logoer og skuespillerbilleder på forhånd i de størrelser, jeres apps faktisk bruger. Nye film og afsnit klares et par minutter efter, de er kommet ind. Opgaven sætter farten ned, når nogen bruger serveren. Første kørsel på et stort bibliotek tager et par timer.
- "Mere som dette" og samlinger på detaljesider huskes i 30 minutter pr. bruger. Jellyfin 12 bruger op til 1,5 sekund på at regne dem ud hver gang. De glemmes, så snart du ser eller markerer noget som favorit, eller biblioteket ændres.
- Søgningen henter skuespillere og instruktørens andre film, når du holder pause i skrivningen, i stedet for ved hvert tastetryk. Skuespillerne vises, så snart de er kendt, uden at vente på instruktørens film, billeder længere ude i rækkerne hentes først, når de kommer frem, og søger du på det samme igen, står det der med det samme.
- Mens plakater og portrætter hentes, vises en sløret udgave af billedet i stedet for en tom grå boks.
- Det hele kan slås fra under Speed i indstillingerne.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Afsnitsnummeret er tilbage på forsiden på Jellyfin 12.

- Når en serie har fået et nyt afsnit, viser Jellyfin 12 selve afsnittets kort i "Nyligt tilføjet" i stedet for seriens kort med antallet af usete afsnit. Det tal var det, New Badges skrev S/E-nummeret ind i, så mærket forsvandt. Afsnitskortene får nu selv et mærke med fx S4E7 samme sted og i samme stil.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Ingen dobbelt "Anmod om film eller serie" i sidemenuen på Jellyfin 12.

- Seerr Requests har sin egen Tilføj-knap i sidemenuen lige ovenover, så genvejen fra New Badges var den samme knap to gange. På Jellyfin 12 vises den ikke længere.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.0.0, hvor genvejen stadig findes.

Forsiden indlæses hurtigere.

- NEW-badges husker datoerne et kvarter, så forsiden ikke slår hver serie op igen, hver gang appen åbnes.
- Højst tre serieopslag ad gangen, så plakaterne ikke står i kø bag dem.
- Trending og den samlede Fortsæt-række vises med det samme fra sidste besøg og opdateres i baggrunden - også efter appen har været lukket.
- Samme række hentes ikke længere to gange på én gang.
- Om Seerr Requests er installeret, huskes et døgn.
- Scriptet caches af browseren og hentes kun igen, når plugin'et er opdateret.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.0.0.

Sidemenuen bliver nu lukket, når du bruger den på Jellyfin 12 - også efter genvejen til anmodninger, "Overrask mig" og Fortsæt med at se.

2.6.1.0 fik det ikke helt løst. Jellyfin 12 lukker selv sidemenuen, så snart du trykker på noget i den, og menuens baggrund virker som en kontakt: lukkes den en gang til, åbner den igen. Når New Badges eller Seerr Requests bagefter også lukkede menuen, sprang den derfor op igen. Nu lukker New Badges kun menuen, hvis den stadig er helt fremme, og genvejen til anmodninger holder Seerr Requests' ekstra lukning væk.

Genvejene i menuen har nu præcis samme skrift og placering som Jellyfins egne punkter.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.0.0, som virker uændret.

Sidemenuen lukker nu rigtigt når du bruger genvejen til anmodninger på Jellyfin 12, og genvejene i menuen har fået samme skrift som resten af menuen.

Genvejen til anmodninger åbnede den rigtige fane, men sidemenuen blev stående åben. Både New Badges og Seerr Requests lukkede menuen, lige efter hinanden - og en ekstra lukning mens menuen stadig er ved at glide ud, åbner den igen i stedet. Nu lukkes den kun én gang.

"Overrask mig" og genvejen til anmodninger stod med en anden, fed skrift end resten af menuen. De bruger nu samme skrift, størrelse og placering som Hjem og Favoritter.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.0.0, som virker uændret.

Fire funktioner der holdt op med at virke på Jellyfin 12 virker igen, og NEW-mærket sidder ikke længere på skuespillere.

NEW på skuespillere og instruktører: Rækken "Cast & Crew" på en films side fik NEW på alle kort. En person i Jellyfin får en ny oprettelsesdato hver gang dens oplysninger opdateres, så alle skuespillere så nyligt tilføjede ud. Personer får aldrig NEW nu. Den fejl fandtes også på 10.11.

Genvejene i sidemenuen (hurtigsøgning, "Fortsæt afspilning", "Overrask mig" og genvejen til anmodninger): Jellyfin 12 har lavet sidemenuen om, og den gamle menu findes stadig i siden men bliver aldrig vist - så genvejene blev lagt et sted ingen kunne se dem. De sidder nu i den nye menu, lige under Hjem og Favoritter. Jellyfin 12 viser kun den menu på smalle skærme som telefoner.

Genvejen til anmodninger åbnede i nogle tilfælde Udgivelseskalenderen i stedet for anmodningssiden. Den rammer nu den rigtige fane.

Filmbibliotekets nye forside: Jellyfin 12 har ingen faneblade på filmsiden, og det var netop fanebladet forsiden blev sat ind i. Den dukker nu op igen i stedet for Jellyfins eget gitter.

Hurtigsøgningen: Søgeknappen i toppen er en ny knap på Jellyfin 12, så et klik gik direkte til Jellyfins egen søgeside. Den åbner nu hurtigsøgningen igen.

Eget logo i toppen: Hvis du har sat et logo op, vises det nu igen i stedet for servernavnet i den nye topbjælke.

Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan kun installeres der. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.0.0, som virker uændret.

Indstillingssiden er tegnet om, så den ser ud som resten af Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin 12 har lavet sine egne indstillingssider om: felterne er nu fyldte bokse med en lille etiket øverst i selve feltet, i stedet for en label ovenover. Denne side fulgte stadig den gamle stil og stak derfor ud fra alt andet i dashboardet.

Felter, afkrydsningsfelter, overskrifter og Gem-knappen matcher nu Jellyfin 12's egne — samme højde, samme afrunding, samme farver. Farverne hentes fra Jellyfin 12's eget tema, så siden også følger med hvis du skifter tema.

Kun udseende. Der er ikke ændret noget i hvad siden gør, eller i indstillingerne selv. På Jellyfin 10.11 ser siden ud præcis som før — den nye stil slås kun til, hvis serveren rent faktisk er 12.

Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende adgangsnøglen på (X-Emby-Token), så alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt. Uden det svarede serveren 401.

Indstillingssiden kunne ikke åbnes på Jellyfin 12. Pluginet kørte, men dets side under Dashboard → Plugins var der ikke, og der stod ingen fejl nogen steder. Jellyfin 12's nye dashboard viser kun siden, hvis den selv beder om at komme i menuen.

Accentfarven læses nu direkte fra temaet. Før blev den gættet ved at male en usynlig knap med Jellyfins egne klasser og aflæse farven — men Jellyfin 12 tegner sine knapper på en ny måde hvor den klasse ikke findes, så gættet slog fejl og faldt tilbage til en fast farve.

Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan kun installeres der. Kører du stadig 10.11, bliver du på den forrige udgave, som virker uændret — serveren vælger selv den rigtige. Grunden til at der skal være to: 10.11 og 12 kører på hver sin udgave af .NET, så det samme build kan ikke køre begge steder.

# 🧭 Plugin Pages, Ready for Jellyfin 12 Plugin Pages **3.0.0.0** brings the plugin forward for **Jellyfin 12**, updating the way custom pages are injected into the Jellyfin web client and fixing the user-facing plugin settings flow for Jellyfin's latest architecture. This release also drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7**, while introducing a new plugin-facing API that makes it much easier for other plugins to add and manage their own pages. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12**. * Added a new public **Plugin Interface** allowing other plugins to register pages programmatically through `PluginInterface.RegisterPage(JObject)`. * Added `PluginInterface.RemovePage(string id)`, allowing plugins to unregister pages they previously registered. * Updated Plugin Pages' web-client injection to work with the changes introduced in Jellyfin 12. * Updated user-facing plugin settings pages to work with Jellyfin 12. * Updated the underlying Jellyfin dependencies and integration points required by the new server/web-client architecture. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Reworked page injection to account for changes to the Jellyfin 12 web client. * Improved compatibility for plugins that use Plugin Pages to expose user-facing pages inside Jellyfin. * Updated the user plugin settings integration so pages opened through Jellyfin's user menu continue to behave correctly on Jellyfin 12. * Dependent plugins can now manage their pages at runtime rather than directly modifying Plugin Pages' configuration. * Cleaned up legacy compatibility code that is no longer required now that older Jellyfin versions are being dropped. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed custom plugin pages failing to inject correctly into the **Jellyfin 12** web client. * Fixed user-facing plugin settings pages not working correctly on Jellyfin 12. * Fixed cases where pages registered through Plugin Pages could result in a **Page not found** experience after Jellyfin web-client changes. * Fixed compatibility issues caused by changes to Jellyfin's client-side routing and page-loading behaviour. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility Plugin Pages now provides a public plugin-facing API for registering and removing pages. * `PluginInterface.RegisterPage(JObject)` can be used to register a page directly with Plugin Pages. * The supplied `JObject` is deserialised into Plugin Pages' `PluginPage` model and registered immediately with the page manager. * `PluginInterface.RemovePage(string id)` can be used to unregister an existing page by its ID. * Plugins no longer need to directly modify `Jellyfin.Plugin.PluginPages/config.json` in order to dynamically add their own pages. * Plugins can now register pages during startup and remove them again during shutdown or when their configuration changes. This should be considered the **preferred integration path for dependent plugins going forward**, replacing direct manipulation of Plugin Pages' configuration where possible. The new API is additive, so existing configuration-based integrations are not inherently broken by the update. Plugin developers are, however, encouraged to migrate to the new interface for cleaner lifecycle management and better compatibility with future Plugin Pages releases. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12**. * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier Plugin Pages release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Plugin Pages continues to require a compatible version of **File Transformation**. * Plugins that depend on Plugin Pages should also be updated to versions compatible with Jellyfin 12. * The new `PluginInterface` is additive; plugins using the previous configuration-based approach can continue to work, but the programmatic API is now the recommended integration method. ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

## ✨ New Features

- **Notify chosen users**: tick non-admin users on the new **Settings** tab to show them the badge too.
- **Counts only**: they see how many plugins changed, and can't dismiss or restart.

## 🎨 Improvements

- **Tabbed plugin page**: the page is split into **Updates** and **Settings** tabs.

## ✨ New Features

- **Notify chosen users**: tick non-admin users on the new **Settings** tab to show them the badge too.
- **Counts only**: they see how many plugins changed, and can't dismiss or restart.

## 🎨 Improvements

- **Tabbed plugin page**: the page is split into **Updates** and **Settings** tabs.

## ✨ New Features

- **Removals are tracked**: uninstalling a plugin now shows on the **Plugin Updates** page and badges your avatar, just like an install, until the restart that applies it.
- **History of applied changes**: a collapsible **Previously applied** section lists what earlier restarts made live, grouped by restart. It keeps the last 50 changes and can be cleared.
- **Built for Jellyfin 12.0 and 12.1**: each release is now published once per server version, so the catalog offers a build that targets your server exactly.

## 🐞 Bug Fixes

- **One card per plugin**: installing and then updating a plugin before a restart shows as a single change, and installing then removing one shows nothing at all.
- **Manual task runs are safe**: running the plugin's startup task by hand from Scheduled Tasks no longer clears changes that are still waiting for a restart.
- **Sturdier saved state**: a damaged state file is kept aside as `updates.json.unreadable` instead of being overwritten, and one bad entry no longer costs the rest.

## 🐞 Bug Fixes

- **Nothing runs for non-admins**: the script checks who you are first, instead of every user's browser polling once a minute for an admin-only answer.
- **Far fewer checks**: every five minutes instead of every minute, and paused while the tab is in the background.
- **Smaller checks**: each check now asks only for the number it needs, instead of downloading every plugin's full release notes and throwing them away.
- **Switching tabs is free**: returning to the Jellyfin tab no longer triggers a fresh check.
- **Lighter on the browser**: the plugin now only keeps an eye on the page while a notification is actually showing, rather than constantly, for everyone.

## 📋 Notes

- The badge can now take up to five minutes to appear after a plugin is updated, rather than up to one. Opening the user menu always shows the current count.

## ✨ New Features

- **Plugin icon**: the plugin now has its own icon in the catalog and in your plugin list, instead of a blank placeholder.

## 🐞 Bug Fixes

- **Readable changelogs**: a plugin's release notes on the **Plugin Updates** page now appear properly formatted. Bold text, headings and links show as intended, instead of displaying the raw formatting characters around them.

## 📋 Notes

- Nothing to reconfigure. Updating takes only the usual restart.
- Still Jellyfin 12 only. The avatar badge and profile-menu entry need the [JavaScript Injector](https://github.com/n00bcodr/Jellyfin-JavaScript-Injector) plugin; the dashboard page works without it.

## Plugin Update Notifier 1.0.0.0

First release, for Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin installs plugin updates in place but only applies them on the next server restart, and nothing in the UI tells an administrator that a restart is pending. This plugin closes that gap: it watches plugin install and update events and surfaces a clear, dismissible reminder until the server is restarted.

### Features

- Avatar badge: a dot appears on the admin's profile avatar the moment a plugin change leaves a restart pending.
- Profile-menu entry: a "Plugin Updates" item in the user dropdown, shown only to administrators, with a count of what changed.
- Dashboard page: lists every changed plugin, its old and new version, the release changelog, and a link to each plugin's source.
- Shared dismiss: dismissing hides the reminder for every admin session, not just one browser; a later plugin change brings it back.
- Self-clearing: the reminder disappears on its own after the restart it was asking for.

### Requirements

- Jellyfin 12 (this release uses APIs not present in 10.x).
- The avatar badge and profile-menu entry additionally require the [JavaScript Injector](https://github.com/n00bcodr/Jellyfin-JavaScript-Injector) plugin (4.0.0.0 or newer). The dashboard page works without it.

versions.changelog: If the plugin stopped working with "The poster overlay state file ... could not be read", this release is for you. The state file is now written atomically, so a server that dies mid-write can no longer leave it empty - which is what happened on the reference server when the VM was killed during the nightly run. An image uploaded just before a crash is now recognised on the next run, and a cached original without a record is never overwritten. New task "Rebuild poster overlay state": run it with the dry run on first. It rebuilds a record only where drawing today's badges onto the cached original gives the cover on the item again, and lists everything else by name without touching it. Do not delete a damaged state file - the old error message advised that, and it was wrong.

Nothing changes visibly in this one. The preview picker on the settings page now tells the server explicitly not to substitute collections for the films inside them when searching. That was already the behaviour, but only because Jellyfin happens to switch it off for searches by itself - and because the search box never queries with fewer than two characters. Neither is something this plugin controls, so it now says what it means. Badges, rendering and the scheduled task are untouched.

The report about folder names that disagree with the video stream over HDR is now a setting, and it is off by default. It only says something if your folder names carry release tags - if you name folders "Film (Year)", every HDR title would be counted as a disagreement. Turn it on under Operation if the tags are there. The badges follow the video stream either way, with the report on or off.

Names the file behind "the image could not be decoded" instead of only the film, so a broken cover can be found without searching by hand - and fixes a case where that message could not be reached at all, because the renderer threw on a file its decoder cannot open rather than reporting it. The HDR/DV disagreement between folder name and video stream is now summarised once per run instead of printed for every film: it is the ordinary case, not an exception, and it was burying the messages worth reading. The v12 build now targets Jellyfin 12.0.0 rather than a release candidate.

Fixes a badge that could not be taken off again. When an item lost its last badge - a duplicate was deleted, or it never really had a twin - the plugin was supposed to put the untouched cover back, and never did: the restore asked for a lock its own caller was already holding, then failed silently. A run with 222 items to restore restored none of them and reported a missing cache that was present. If your library carries labels that no longer apply, the next nightly run clears them.

Fixes the audio badge appearing on films that have no second copy at all.

Peers were matched by any shared provider id, which swept in TmdbCollection - an id every film of a series carries. All fifteen Star Wars films therefore counted as copies of one another, their audio formats differed, and a badge appeared where the rule says there should be none. Only ids that name a title are used now: IMDb, TMDb, TVDB and the custom id an NFO can set.

Also fixes the badge never appearing in the previous version, where copies were grouped by Jellyfin's presentation key. That key groups the rows of a series, but for a film it falls back to the item's own id unless the files were merged as alternate versions by hand, so two ordinary copies never shared it.

The badge itself is unchanged: ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on, drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it, describing the track in the language you set rather than the technically best one.

Fixes the audio badge never appearing. It was grouping copies of a film by Jellyfin's presentation key, which groups the rows of a series but not of a film: for a film that key falls back to the item's own id unless the files were merged as alternate versions by hand, so two ordinary copies never shared it and the badge was skipped every time. Copies are now matched by provider id.

The badge itself is unchanged: ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on, drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it, and describing the track in the language you set rather than the technically best one.

Adds an audio-format badge - ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on - drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it. Off by default.

The restriction is the point. Measured on a library of 2,346 films: of 105 groups holding more than one copy of a film, 7 differ in nothing the existing badges could show except the audio format. Every other film has no second copy at all, so a format badge there describes a file nobody is comparing to anything.

Which track it describes is configurable, as a list of languages, best first - the first one any track carries wins. This matters more than it sounds: 437 films carry several languages in different formats, typically a German AC3 beside an English DTS, and taking the best track badges such a film "DTS", which is true about the file and about a track its owner never selects. Setting a language therefore draws fewer badges rather than more, which is the intent.

Spelling is forgiving because the server is asked rather than a table in the plugin: "de", "ger", "deu" and "German" all name one language, for every language Jellyfin knows. A file with a single track always reports that one, whatever the preference says.

Within the chosen language only the best track counts - a film with Atmos, a DTS-HD track and a stereo commentary is an Atmos film. The label carries as much as the job needs: where two copies are both plain DTS and differ only in the channel layout, the layout is added.

The setting for merging Dolby Vision and HDR is now spelled MergeDolbyVisionAndHDR in code. Stored configurations are unaffected - the file keeps the old spelling on purpose, so a value anybody switched off stays switched off.

Adds an audio-format badge - ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on - drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it. Off by default.

Every other film has no second copy at all, so a format badge there describes a file nobody is comparing to anything.

A file with a single track always reports that one, whatever the preference says. Spelling is forgiving, since ISO 639-2 gives several languages two codes and files in the wild use both.

Adds an audio-format badge - ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on - and draws it only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it. Off by default.

The restriction is the point. Measured on a library of 2,346 films: of 105 groups that hold more than one copy of a film, 7 differ in nothing the existing badges could show except the audio format. Every other film has no second copy at all, so a format badge there says something true about a file nobody is comparing to anything.

The label carries as much as the job needs. The format alone settles most cases; where two copies are both plain DTS and differ only in the channel layout, the layout is added. Where even that is equal nothing is drawn, because "two audio tracks" is not something a badge can usefully say. Only the best track counts - a film with Atmos, a DTS-HD track and a stereo commentary is an Atmos film.

Grouping follows Jellyfin's own presentation key, the one it uses to decide which rows are shown as a single tile, rather than an id read out of the provider list.

The setting for merging Dolby Vision and HDR into one pill is now spelled MergeDolbyVisionAndHDR in code. Stored configurations are unaffected: the file keeps the old spelling on purpose, so a value anybody had switched off stays switched off.

The pinned preview - the copy of the picture at the right edge of the window - could be closed and then not reopened. There is a labelled button beside the style buttons now, and whether you want the panel is remembered between visits.

Also finishes a correction from the previous version. Twelve style rules were applying to the whole Jellyfin interface rather than to the plugin's own settings page, four of them since long before the preview existed. Nothing collided in practice, which is why it would have gone on unnoticed. There are no exceptions: an earlier attempt claimed the pinned panel sits outside the page and could not be scoped, which was reasoned rather than checked - it is a child of the page, and being fixed-position does not change that.

Fixes the preview opening at the poster's stored size and covering the settings page. Only the previous version is affected - the preview arrived there.

A percentage limit on the image was no limit at all in that spot: it resolves against its container, and the floating panel is fixed-position with no width of its own, so the container simply grew with the picture. The panel now has a width, and the image is bounded in both directions, since a poster arrives at 1000x1500 and upwards.

Also corrects eight style rules that were applying to the whole Jellyfin interface rather than to the plugin's own settings page. Nothing collided in practice, which is why it would otherwise have gone unnoticed. Two rules genuinely have to reach outside the page and now say so; the rest are scoped, and both facts are held in place by tests.

The settings page now previews on a real item, drawn by the server through exactly the code a run uses. It used to imitate the badges in SVG on a mock poster - a second implementation of the drawing rules, which had already drifted from the real one: the centred positions had to be taught to both, and the imitation estimated text width where the renderer measures it, so no pill was ever quite the right width.

The page sends the settings as they stand, saved or not, so a change can be looked at before it is kept. Nothing is written while previewing - not the item, not the cached original, not the stored configuration.

Two things come with using a real item. There is a search box to choose which one, and on opening the page offers one that already carries badges, because picking at random would usually show an untouched poster and look like a fault. And when no badge is drawn the page now says why - the category is off, the item is on the exception list, or the episode has no second copy and the category only badges where that tells two apart. An unbadged preview and a broken one used to look identical.

The settings sections fold away and remember how they were left.

For anyone driving the plugin from a script: POST PosterOverlays/Preview/{itemId} takes a configuration and returns the image it would produce, changing nothing, with the badge count and any explanation in the X-PosterOverlays-Badges and X-PosterOverlays-Note headers.

Housekeeping, with no change to how badges are drawn: the plugin now appears under "Movies & Shows" in the catalogue instead of "General", which is where something that draws on the posters of films, series, seasons and episodes belongs.

The category is not free text. The official catalogue uses exactly eight values, and one outside that set parses cleanly and then belongs to no filter at all - the plugin would quietly drop out of every category view with no error anywhere. The build now refuses a value outside those eight before it starts, rather than shipping one and finding out later.

Only the repository manifest is actually read for this, so it could have been changed without a release. It goes out as a version so the copy inside the package says the same thing: that copy is never displayed, but it does sit in the ZIP, so leaving the two apart would mean the package permanently disagrees with the catalogue it is listed in.

Added: two centred badge positions, "Top, centred" and "Bottom, centred", for images a client crops on the sides. Jellyfin's episode list shows a still in a container of its own proportions and takes the difference off the left and right, so a badge near either edge is cut in half - and raising the margin does not help, because the crop is proportional rather than a fixed number of pixels.

Centred sidesteps that instead of fighting it: the crop may take as much as it likes off both sides and a badge in the middle stays whole, so only the vertical distance still has to fit. The horizontal margin is ignored in these two positions, because a margin is a distance from an edge and there is none. With a vertical badge direction each pill is centred on its own rather than the column as a block.

Existing presets are unaffected: the new values are appended, so the four corners keep the meaning they had.

Added: "Kino Fassung" written as two words is now recognised as the theatrical cut. The catalogue only knew the compound spelling, so a folder that separated the words got no edition badge at all and instead turned up in the nightly report of edition-looking phrases with no rule for them. The optional space cannot widen the match - "kino" on its own still fires no rule.

Documented: the repair path never downloads from an image provider that is switched off for the library the item belongs to, and the code now says why that is not automatic. Passing the item does not restrict the providers by itself; "disabled" is defined relative to a library, so the item supplies the frame of reference and the query flag applies it. No behaviour change - the guard was already there, but it read like tidiness somebody could remove.

Changed: a folder that says two independent things now gets two edition badges. "REMASTERED.EXTENDED" used to draw EXT alone, because both rules matched and only the first was ever used.

Collecting every match would be wrong the other way round - it would turn "Extended Directors Cut" into three badges for one version. So each rule now declares what kind of statement it makes: which cut this is, how the picture is framed or coloured, how the copy was mastered. Within one kind the first match still wins, so a combination like EDC stays a single badge; across kinds the badges stand side by side, with the cut first because that is what tells two copies of a film apart.

Measured over 2380 real folders, six carry two edition tokens and no folder carries two of the same kind, so this is a small and predictable change.

Added: episodes are read from their file name, so two copies of one episode in the same resolution can finally be told apart. A movie keeps its release tags in its folder name, but a flattened season is one folder with every episode beside each other in it, so for episodes the file name is the only place they live. The episode title is subtracted first, exactly as a film title is - otherwise an ordinary title like "The Extended Family" would be read as an edition - and the remaining text must contain a known release tag or it is discarded whole. Movies are unaffected.

Added: records whose item no longer exists are cleared at the end of the nightly run, together with their cached originals. Until now they stayed on disk forever. This matters more than tidiness, because repairing a wrong metadata match recreates the entry under a new id. The sweep refuses to act when the library looks wrong rather than smaller, since a cached original is the only copy of an unbadged cover.

Fixed: the two completeness colour swatches showed black and picking a colour had no effect. The presets held empty strings written by an earlier load-time fault, and a colour input with no value renders as black - so an absence looked like a choice. A blank colour is now filled in with the default, and every reader of a colour treats blank and the default alike, so repairing the stored value redraws nothing.

Fixed: ticking "Color the badge by whether it holds throughout" looked like it showed the preview twice. It was showing both halves of that setting; both rows are captioned now.

Fixed: the step buttons beside the numeric fields are smaller and properly centred.

Fixes the settings page writing blanks over the selected preset while it was still loading - which is how a preset ended up named Unnamed with settings nobody chose. The number fields no longer rely on the browser spinner: it is replaced by two buttons so the spacing is actually set. Adds a floating preview pinned to the right edge that shows the selected style while it is being edited.

Fixes the settings page throwing the presets away on save. A plugin configuration travels through two serialisers: XmlSerializer writes the file and populates a read-only collection property, System.Text.Json carries it to and from the settings page and silently does not. The presets were on disk and on the page, and gone the moment Save was pressed, leaving every category pointing at a preset that no longer existed. A configuration already emptied by this repairs itself from the legacy settings, rebuilt under the same preset id, so the look key is unchanged and nothing already badged is redrawn. Also proper spacing between a number and its spinner arrows, a colour picker beside each completeness colour, and a preset saved without a name becomes Unnamed rather than an invisible entry.

Presets: how a badge looks is now a named preset that any category points at, with four read-only built-ins, duplicate-to-edit, and export/import of presets as JSON. Series, seasons and episodes are badged: what a series may claim is aggregated from its episodes, with several copies of one episode collapsed to the best first, so a show that is available throughout in 4K is not reported as mixed. Where it is genuinely mixed the badge is marked, by colour and by a marker that keeps the label readable. Episodes are badged only where two rows carry the same episode and nothing else tells them apart. Existing settings migrate unchanged: the movie look key is byte-identical, so nothing already badged is redrawn.

Rebuilds the repair task. It no longer searches for an inconsistent cache - that cannot find the damage, because a cache written by the faulty first release is consistent with its own record and merely describes an already badged image. It now works on scope: every item with a record plus every item that would be badged gets a fresh primary image from the metadata provider and is forgotten, so a following apply run badges it once, cleanly. A single-item route allows trying it on one poster first.

Internal correctness: everything the plugin and its build script persist now uses the invariant culture and ISO 8601 UTC explicitly. The build script formatted its timestamp without a culture, which is only correct on a machine whose culture uses a colon as the time separator - 21 do not. Nothing about the badges changes.

Changing the look of the badges now redraws the posters that already have them. Only the badge set was compared before, so a new style, corner, direction or size was reported as "already correct" and never applied to anything that was already done. Settings that do not change the image are kept out of that comparison, so saving an exclusion list does not order a redraw of the whole library.

Settings page layout: the exception boxes and the checkbox rows no longer depend on custom elements that a plugin page cannot rely on being registered, number fields are narrow and right aligned, and the three style previews replace the style dropdown instead of duplicating it.

Fixes the settings page, which did not initialise at all: its root element pointed at a controller module that does not exist instead of declaring the controls it needs, so nothing was upgraded and no value was ever loaded. Adds a 3D badge as its own category, so a film can be an extended cut and in 3D at the same time. Adds a direction setting, so the badges can run along the top or bottom edge in one row instead of stacking downwards. Adds a live preview of all three styles on the settings page.

Fixes a defect that drew a second badge on top of the first: the scheduled task and the image-change watcher kept separate state, so the watcher treated an image the task had just badged as an untouched original. One shared state, written after every item. A cached original whose hash no longer matches is now refused for drawing and for restoring, and a new "Repair poster overlays" task fetches a fresh cover from the metadata provider for those items. The settings page could not be saved at all - numeric option values where the server expects enum names, empty number fields becoming null, and no error handler, so a failed save showed as an endless spinner. The badge order is now configurable and sortable.

First release. Draws the edition, the resolution and the video range onto the primary image so two entries of the same film can be told apart on the tile, and re-applies the badge whenever a provider replaces the cover. Leave the dry run switch on for the first pass.

Posterizarr.description: Local asset metadata provider and real-time WebSocket sync engine. Instantly maps and updates posters, backgrounds, seasons, and title cards without library scans.
Posterizarr.overview: A companion plugin for Posterizarr that maps local assets to Jellyfin library items and connects to Posterizarr's real-time WebSocket stream (/ws/events) to instantaneously apply rendered artwork in under a second.

versions.changelog: Official Release 3.3.7

Official Release 3.3.6

- **BoxSet & Collection Support**: Added Primary, Thumbnail, and Backdrop image resolution for collections across Jellyfin and Emby.
- **Asset Path Resolution**: Resolves Collections directory at root or within subfolders, supporting both nested folders and flat file structures.
- **Smart Name Normalization**: Handles '[boxset]' tag stripping, '&' vs 'and' variants, illegal character sanitization, and automatic 'Collection' suffix matching.
- **Metadata Refresh Detection**: Implemented HasChanged check using file timestamps so library refreshes detect updated assets on disk.
- **Real-Time WebSocket Sync**: Added collection asset handling to automatically invalidate cache and update artwork via WebSocket stream.
- **Opt-In Setting**: Added UpdateCollection configuration toggle (default false) in plugin configuration page.
Official Release 3.3.5

Official Release 3.3.4

- **WebSocket Real-Time Sync**: Added background listener service connecting to `/ws/events` for instant image updates.
- **Direct Image Application**: Streams and persists image updates directly using internal provider APIs upon receiving events.
- **Enhanced Configuration Page**: Added Real-Time Sync toggle, Posterizarr URL input, and API key configuration with live connection test diagnostics.
- **Volume Latency Tolerance**: Added 2-second retry loop for newly created image files.
- **Catalog Image**: Configured `imageUrl` in repository manifests.

Official Release 3.3.3

- **Persistent State Caching**: Added `posterizarr_sync_cache.json` in the plugin data directory to track file sizes, timestamps, and image metadata. Unchanged assets are skipped instantly in memory with zero network I/O.
- **Directory & File Caching**: Added `AssetPathResolver` to cache root library shares and folder file listings. Reduces tens of thousands of remote SMB/NFS round-trips to a single query per media folder.
- **Parallel Async Sync Task**: Upgraded `PosterizarrSyncTask` to use `Parallel.ForEachAsync` with adaptive concurrency, replacing single-threaded sequential processing.
- **Tiered Image Verification**: Added 4KB header and file-length pre-checks to eliminate continuous ~30 MB/s full-file MD5 hash calculations across the network.
- **Debug Mode Toggle**: Debug messages (`[Posterizarr DEBUG]`) are now directly controlled by the plugin's `EnableDebugMode` setting and visible in the Jellyfin log viewer without changing server logging configurations.
- **Emby Optimization**: Added same-path timestamp comparison to prevent double-hashing identical local files in Emby.
- **Performance Benchmark**: Successfully verified on a 39,000-item library, reducing task runtime from **32m 51s to 13 seconds (~151x faster)** with near-zero network and disk utilization.

Official Release 3.3.2

- **Jellyfin 12.0.x & 10.11.x Multi-Targeting**: Compiled for both `.NET 9` (Jellyfin 10.11.x) and `.NET 10` (Jellyfin 12.0.x) with target-specific ABI dependencies (`10.11.0.0` and `12.0.0.0`).
- **Automated Dual Packaging**: Manifest and release pipelines now generate separate distribution archives (`Posterizarr.Plugin_v3.3.2.zip` and `Posterizarr.Plugin_v3.3.2-jf12.zip`).
- **Emby API Token Authentication**: Updated media server logo upload headers to use `MediaBrowser Token="{token}"` format, resolving upload failures on Emby servers.
