PostgreSQL Database Provider.description: Production-ready PostgreSQL backend for Jellyfin. Bidirectional SQLite migration, near-instant search, health diagnostics, read-only SQL console and scheduled maintenance — no core modifications required.
PostgreSQL Database Provider.overview: Reemplaza SQLite por PostgreSQL como motor de base de datos de Jellyfin. Incluye migración bidireccional SQLite↔PostgreSQL, búsqueda casi instantánea con índices GIN, health check automático al arrancar, consola SQL de solo lectura, mantenimiento programado (VACUUM/REINDEX/Backup) y un host seguro de esquemas privados para otros plugins.

versions.changelog:
## Español

### 3.0.4 — Fechas, búsqueda, guardado y migración

- Corrige el cierre de Jellyfin Android TV al abrir bibliotecas: el caché de consultas descartaba `DateTimeKind.Utc` al bufferizar y el cliente recibía fechas sin zona horaria, que sustituía por su valor mínimo y hacían fallar la conversión. Las columnas de fecha se bufferizan como UTC y el lector restaura el `Kind` como segunda barrera.
- Nueva migración que normaliza fechas no finitas o mínimas ya guardadas en `BaseItems`, y normalización de los centinelas `DateTime` y `DateTimeOffset` antes de escribir.
- La búsqueda deja de distinguir mayúsculas y minúsculas e incluye título visible, título original y título para ordenar, con índice trigram sobre `SortName`.
- Corrige el error 500 al abrir la ficha de un artista o persona: las filas duplicadas se resuelven con una actualización sin cambios sobre la clave primaria en lugar de `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, que informaba 0 filas y EF Core trataba como conflicto de concurrencia.
- Corrige la migración SQLite → PostgreSQL: se conserva el historial de rutinas de código ya aplicadas, identificadas por el nombre de la migración. Sin él, Jellyfin volvía a ejecutar rutinas que esperan `library.db` y el arranque fallaba con `no such table: TypedBaseItems` (#9).
- El proveedor fija `QuerySplittingBehavior` en `SingleQuery`, igual que el proveedor SQLite, y deja de llenar el log con `MultipleCollectionIncludeWarning`.

Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 o posterior y .NET 10.

---

## English

### 3.0.4 — Dates, search, saving, and migration

- Fixes Jellyfin Android TV crashing when a library is opened: the query cache dropped `DateTimeKind.Utc` while buffering, so the client received dates without a time zone, replaced them with its minimum value, and failed converting it. Date columns are buffered as UTC and the reader restores the `Kind` as a second safeguard.
- New migration that normalizes non-finite or minimum dates already stored in `BaseItems`, plus normalization of `DateTime` and `DateTimeOffset` sentinels before writing.
- Search is no longer case-sensitive and now covers display, original, and sort titles, with a trigram index on `SortName`.
- Fixes the 500 returned when opening an artist or person page: duplicate rows are resolved with a no-op update on the primary key instead of `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, which reported zero affected rows and EF Core treated as a concurrency conflict.
- Fixes the SQLite → PostgreSQL migration: the history of code migrations already applied is preserved, matched by migration name. Without it, Jellyfin re-ran routines that expect `library.db` and startup failed with `no such table: TypedBaseItems` (#9).
- The provider pins `QuerySplittingBehavior` to `SingleQuery`, matching Jellyfin's SQLite provider, and stops flooding the log with `MultipleCollectionIncludeWarning`.

Requires Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 or newer, and .NET 10.

## Español

### 3.0.3 — Integraciones privadas, mantenimiento y estabilidad

- Nuevo host seguro para esquemas privados de plugins: registro, migraciones aisladas y acceso sin exponer credenciales ni el esquema `public` de Jellyfin.
- Nueva pestaña **Integraciones** para revisar esquemas registrados, consultar una muestra limitada de datos, ver métricas por tabla y administrar `ANALYZE`, `VACUUM (ANALYZE)` y `REINDEX` por esquema.
- Las tareas programadas mantienen `public` y solo los esquemas privados autorizados por el administrador.
- Health incorpora métricas de presión de buffers, bloques leídos, uso temporal y WAL para diagnosticar consultas lentas.
- Estado actual detecta el motor activo sin esperar la validación SQLite; esta continúa en segundo plano y se vuelve a comprobar antes de revertir.
- Se refuerza el aislamiento de identificadores en operaciones de exploración y mantenimiento de esquemas privados.
- Documentación actualizada en español e inglés, incluida la integración para desarrolladores, exportación SQLite segura y orientación para Docker.

Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 o posterior y .NET 10.

---

## English

### 3.0.3 — Private integrations, maintenance, and stability

- New secure host for private plugin schemas: registration, isolated migrations, and storage without exposing credentials or Jellyfin's `public` schema.
- New **Integrations** tab to review registered schemas, inspect a bounded data sample, view per-table metrics, and manage `ANALYZE`, `VACUUM (ANALYZE)`, and `REINDEX` per schema.
- Scheduled tasks maintain `public` and only private schemas explicitly enabled by an administrator.
- Health adds buffer-pressure, blocks-read, temporary-I/O, and WAL metrics for slow-query diagnosis.
- Current status detects the active engine without waiting for SQLite validation; validation continues in the background and is checked again before rollback.
- Strengthens identifier isolation in private-schema exploration and maintenance operations.
- Updated Spanish and English documentation, including developer integration, safe SQLite export, and Docker guidance.

Requires Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 or newer, and .NET 10.

## Español

### 3.0.2 — Estabilidad, integridad y exportación segura

- Corrige la normalización de `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset` y arreglos antes de escribir en PostgreSQL, evitando errores de Npgsql por `Kind` incompatible.
- Las escrituras concurrentes de `UserData` y las actualizaciones completas de elementos usan upserts atómicos para reducir conflictos durante actualizaciones bajo demanda.
- La activación de PostgreSQL valida la conexión antes de modificar `database.xml`.
- Se elimina la restauración automática de backups y la restauración manual no reemplaza objetos existentes por defecto.
- Las consultas concurrentes idénticas de inicio se consolidan mientras se llena la caché.
- La exportación PostgreSQL → SQLite crea y valida un `library.db` SQLite real; evita el archivo inválido que impedía iniciar Jellyfin.
- La exportación ya no copia ni marca a ciegas el historial de migraciones.

Verificado con Build Release, pruebas unitarias e integración real contra PostgreSQL. Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16+ y .NET 10.

---

## English

### 3.0.2 — Stability, integrity and safe export

- Fixes normalization of `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, and arrays before PostgreSQL writes, avoiding Npgsql errors caused by incompatible `Kind` values.
- Concurrent `UserData` writes and full item updates use atomic upserts to reduce conflicts during on-demand updates.
- PostgreSQL activation validates the connection before changing `database.xml`.
- Automatic backup restore was removed, and manual restore no longer replaces existing objects by default.
- Identical concurrent home-screen queries are coalesced while the cache is populated.
- PostgreSQL → SQLite export creates and validates a real SQLite `library.db`, preventing the invalid file that stopped Jellyfin from starting.
- Export no longer blindly marks or copies migration history.

Verified with a Release build, unit tests, and real PostgreSQL integration tests. Requires Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16+, and .NET 10.

- Fix: el esquema jellytrend no creaba la tabla donde el motor de JellyTrend guarda el perfil de gustos aprendido (user_affinity), asi que ese perfil no quedaba almacenado. El esquema se crea ahora completo (version 4).
- El esquema se comprueba al arrancar: en una instalacion 3.0.0 la tabla que faltaba se crea sola. No hay que recrear el esquema ni reinstalar nada.
- Docs: la seccion de integracion con JellyTrend documenta las dos piezas del contrato: almacen de datos en el esquema jellytrend (fuera de public, para no colarse en las exportaciones a SQLite) y acelerador de consultas con SQL nativo en las recomendaciones (4-10x en bibliotecas grandes).

Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x. Para Jellyfin 10.11.x usa la version 2.0.1.

3.0.0 - Jellyfin 12.1

Adaptacion completa al contrato de proveedores de Jellyfin 12.1. Requiere .NET 10.

Novedades
- Consola SQL de solo lectura en el panel: 10 plantillas de diagnostico, historial en la sesion y rechazo de sentencias que modifiquen datos.
- Opciones avanzadas funcionales: tamano de pool, sentencias preparadas y tiempo de espera se validan, se guardan, se reflejan en el estado actual y se aplican al proveedor.
- Adaptacion al contrato y al runtime de 12.1: resolucion del ensamblado SQLite del servidor, compatibilidad por base de datos y motor de migracion reescrito.

Correcciones
- PurgeDatabase implementado: en 2.x lanzaba NotImplementedException y rompia la restauracion del respaldo completo del sistema.
- Exportacion a SQLite mas robusta: claves primarias verbatim, diagnostico de constraint, limpieza de filas huerfanas y library.db minimo valido para el arranque.

Verificacion
- Suite xUnit con 74 pruebas, incluidas integraciones reales con PostgreSQL 17.
- Auditor de esquema contra el modelo EF del servidor.

Documentacion
- Manual de migracion de Jellyfin 10.11.x a 12.x, novedades frente a 2.0.1 y nota tecnica de la adaptacion, en espanol e ingles.

Compatibilidad
- Jellyfin 12.1.x - PostgreSQL 16+ - .NET 10.
- Para Jellyfin 10.11.x usa la version 2.0.1.

versions.changelog: Fix: re-added missing Pocket ID preset and other small UI fixes

The hardened OIDC rewrite on Jellyfin 12. Hand-rolled OIDC flow with Trust-On-First-Use discovery-endpoint pinning and an SSRF-guarded, DNS-rebind-pinned HTTP client. Account identity keyed on the OIDC subject, in its own identity-map file (migrated out of the plugin config on upgrade). Fail-closed role-to-policy RBAC with a server-wide admission allowlist. OIDC Back-Channel Logout 1.0. Client-secret indirection (Client Secret File / ENV_VAR reference). Auto-managed SSO login button in Branding. Rewritten admin config page. Opt-in, per-provider verified-email account linking that never binds an administrator account. Username/email/display-name/email-verified now fall back to the userinfo endpoint when the ID token omits them. Token-validation failures surface a plain-language reason (expired cert, audience/issuer mismatch, clock drift, JWKS rotation) instead of a bare error. Fixed OIDC-authenticated sessions showing a blank IP in Jellyfin's activity log. Fixed the Manage Library Access checkbox not responding to clicks. No configuration migration required from 2.0.0.0. Renamed to SSO-OIDC-Authentication (was SSO-OIDC Authentication) so the install folder no longer mixes a space with a hyphen; your saved settings are unaffected.

BREAKING: requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer will not load on 10.10/10.11 (stay on 1.0.7.x for those). Retargeted to .NET 10 and rebuilt against the Jellyfin 12.0 plugin API. Removed the vestigial IAuthenticationProvider.HasPassword override (dropped from the interface in 12.0). No functional changes to the OIDC login, RBAC, or Quick Connect flows.

versions.changelog:
Requests og Kalender i burger-menuen.

Når Jellyfin 12 kører med den gamle skuffe - f.eks. med New Badges' burger-knap
på brede skærme - lægges de to links nu også ind der, lige under Hjem. Menuen
lukker af sig selv, når man klikker på dem.

Styres af de indstillinger, der allerede findes (Requests-fanen og
Kalender-fanen). Ingen nye indstillinger.

Kun Jellyfin 12.

- Menupillen øverst findes nu også i et halvt vindue: ikoner, med navnet på den side du er på, og et hint på resten. På en telefon ligger alt i menuen som før.
- Den valgte knap i pillen er hvid i stedet for blå.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Hele topbaren i én knapgruppe på Jellyfin 12.

- Film, Serier og dine andre biblioteker er nu med i knapgruppen, efter Favoritter og før Tilføj og Kalender. Før stod de uden for, så gruppen så ud som en bar, der stoppede halvvejs.
- Det bibliotek, du er inde i, er fyldt ud i gruppen.
- Ingen tynd kant rundt om gruppen længere - over banneret lignede den en rest af den gamle topbar. Gruppen har nu en mørk, let sløret baggrund i stedet.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Ny topbar på Jellyfin 12.

- Hjem, Favoritter, Tilføj og Kalender er samlet i én knapgruppe, hvor den side, du er på, er fyldt ud. Før var Hjem slet ikke med, og den aktive side blev kun vist med blå tekst.
- Kortere navne: "Tilføj" og "Kalender" (på engelsk "Request" og "Calendar"), så topbaren også er plads til på en bærbar.
- Tilføj og Kalender virker nu også fra andre sider end forsiden - før skete der ingenting.
- Rettet: efter at have åbnet Kalender kunne både Tilføj og Kalender stå markeret, og i sidemenuen på mobilen kunne tre punkter være markeret på én gang.
- Rettet: at skifte fra Tilføj eller Kalender til Hjem eller Favoritter kunne vise to faner oven i hinanden.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Forsiden indlæses hurtigere.

- Kalenderens hukommelse - alle de titler, den har set - ligger nu i sin egen fil på serveren i stedet for i plugin-indstillingerne. Indstillingerne hentes af alle browsere ved hver sideindlæsning og var vokset til over 100 KB; nu er de få KB. Flytningen sker af sig selv, når serveren starter.
- Scriptet caches af browseren og hentes kun igen, når plugin'et er opdateret.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Udgivelseskalenderen viser ikke længere gamle film som Point Break og The Godfather.

TMDB registrerer hver gang en film bliver vist på tv eller lagt på en streamingtjeneste - i alle lande. Kalenderen tog den første dato den fandt, så en fransk tv-visning af Point Break fra 1991 dukkede op som en kommende udgivelse. Nu gælder:

- Film der allerede ligger i biblioteket, vises ikke i kalenderen.
- Kalenderen bruger den tidligste streamingdato, ikke den første der står på listen.
- En dato mere end to år efter filmens premiere er en genudgivelse og vises ikke.

Til Jellyfin 12.

"Test forbindelse"-knappen ser nu rigtig ud ved siden af Gem.

Efter sidste udgave var Gem-knappen tegnet om til Jellyfin 12's stil, men "Test forbindelse" lige under den sad tilbage i den gamle grå udgave, så de to knapper så ud til at være lige vigtige.

Den er nu en omridset knap i temaets farve — samme størrelse som Gem, men tydeligt den sekundære af de to, præcis som Jellyfin 12 selv tegner et sådant knappepar.

Kun udseende. Knappen gør nøjagtig det samme som før.

Indstillingssiden er tegnet om, så den ser ud som resten af Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin 12 har lavet sine egne indstillingssider om: felterne er nu fyldte bokse med en lille etiket øverst i selve feltet, i stedet for en label ovenover. Denne side fulgte stadig den gamle stil og stak derfor ud fra alt andet i dashboardet.

Felter, afkrydsningsfelter, overskrifter og Gem-knappen matcher nu Jellyfin 12's egne — samme højde, samme afrunding, samme farver. Farverne hentes fra Jellyfin 12's eget tema, så siden også følger med hvis du skifter tema.

Kun udseende. Der er ikke ændret noget i hvad siden gør, eller i indstillingerne selv. På Jellyfin 10.11 ser siden ud præcis som før — den nye stil slås kun til, hvis serveren rent faktisk er 12.

Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12.

Fanerne "Tilføj Film/Serie" og "Udgivelseskalender" er flyttet med. Jellyfin 12 har lavet hele den øverste menulinje om, og den gamle fanerække findes stadig i siden men bliver aldrig tegnet — så fanerne blev lagt et sted ingen kunne se dem. De sidder nu i den rigtige menulinje sammen med Favoritter, Film og Serier, og i menuen i siden på telefon.

Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende adgangsnøglen på (X-Emby-Token), så alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt. Uden det svarede serveren 401.

Indstillingssiden kunne ikke åbnes på Jellyfin 12. Pluginet kørte, men dets side under Dashboard → Plugins var der ikke, og der stod ingen fejl nogen steder. Jellyfin 12's nye dashboard viser kun siden, hvis den selv beder om at komme i menuen.

Accentfarven læses nu direkte fra temaet. Før blev den gættet ved at male en usynlig knap med Jellyfins egne klasser og aflæse farven — men Jellyfin 12 tegner sine knapper på en ny måde hvor den klasse ikke findes, så gættet slog fejl og faldt tilbage til en fast farve.

Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan kun installeres der. Kører du stadig 10.11, bliver du på den forrige udgave, som virker uændret — serveren vælger selv den rigtige. Grunden til at der skal være to: 10.11 og 12 kører på hver sin udgave af .NET, så det samme build kan ikke køre begge steder.

versions.changelog:
## Developer
- Hidden titles go back to Synced when they return on the source or Removed files leaves Ignore, instead of staying Ignored after the .ignore is removed
- Integration tests cover Removed files set to Ignore, switching between Keep, Delete and Ignore, a user's own .ignore, and a single gone episode
- Integration tests cover updating from 12.2.7.0 and from older versions with the Whitelist

## Developer
- Removed files has a new Ignore option that hides a movie or show folder with a .ignore file once everything in it is gone from the source, and never hides a season on its own
- Hidden titles show again when they come back on the source or when Removed files leaves Ignore, and a .ignore the plugin did not write is never touched
- Waiting deletions are cancelled when Removed files is not Delete, so switching to Keep or Ignore never removes a file
- Deleting a file from the Sync tab keeps its row as Ignored so it is not downloaded again, and queueing it brings it back
- Updating from before 12.2.7 adds API keys and every administrator to the Whitelist once, so servers that pull from this one keep working
- The Servers tab says where to add the Whitelist row when the other server refuses this one
- A server running another Server Sync version never overwrites edits recorded here, and changes for it wait in the queue until both match
- An item a peer changed that is announced more than ten times in ten minutes stops being announced, so two servers can never echo a change forever. Deletions always go out
- Playlist copies are recorded in the sync database, moved over from playlist-copies.json, and rebuilt from their tags after a reset
- Playlist copies keep their tags after Jellyfin refreshes them
- Upkeep forgets copies of deleted playlists and removes replacement backups left next to finished downloads
- Identify names each result after its server
- The README is shorter and the API reference moved to docs/API.md
- The docs say plainly that both servers must keep the same folder structure under each mapped library

## Developer
- Playlists sync between servers for mapped users, with each item matched by its path and items not on this server left out until they arrive
- Playlist edits and deletions are sent as they happen. Pull keeps the parent's copy, Push overrides the other server, and Sync keeps the newest edit
- Playlist sharing and public access are copied when the new Sharing option is on
- Playlist Sync needs a user mapping, and playlists of users without one never leave their server
- Test Connection shows what the key can do on that server, who it belongs to, and whether it may download media
- Test Connection says whether the other server's whitelist lets this key in, and why not
- A standard user's key works for Pull, Push, and Sync, limited to what that user can see and that user's own history, settings, and playlists
- Sync Content skips a server whose key may not download media and logs why
- Check Link reports the access the other server holds for this one
- The sync endpoints only accept administrators from servers on the Servers tab and users on the new Whitelist, each with the locations they may call from
- Whitelist host names are remembered and looked up again when a caller stops matching, so dynamic DNS keeps working
- Refused sync calls are logged with the user, the address, and the reason
- Servers that pull from this one without being on its Servers tab need a Whitelist row after updating
- The plugin's endpoints moved from /ServerSync to /Sync
- Every sync type in Settings shows what a standard user and an administrator can do
- Settings descriptions are shorter, and retries, approvals, and download speed are tables
- Settings groups the sync types under Synchronization
- User Sync and History Sync only use the key's own user when the key is a standard user's
- The new Permissions page in the docs lists what each function needs
- Identify lists every server that has the item, in the Servers tab order, and picking one keeps the item on that server
- The image picker shows the images of every server that has the item, each named after its server
- Log entries strip control characters from values another server sends

## Developer
- Activity entries for changes sent again, paused peers, and rejected requests name the items involved and say why
- Activity entry details start with a capital letter
- Metadata provider image previews load from the server's External URL when one is set, so a server reached at an internal address still shows them

## Developer
- The metadata provider matches by the item's provider ids when the file path does not match, and seasons and episodes by the show's ids with their season and episode numbers
- The metadata provider logs why it found no match for an item
- A server that could not be reached or runs another version is asked again after 30 seconds

## Developer
- Every server in a pool must run the same Server Sync version. Calls from another version are refused, and Check Link names both versions. Update every server together
- Hints are answered with a code that says what the receiver did with them
- Each server tells the others what it wants from them, so changes outside its mapped libraries, users, and filters are never sent
- A change the other server turned away is held back from it for a day, or until the settings on either side change
- A hint for an item a server does not have yet waits up to seven days and applies when the item arrives. The queue view shows these as waiting for the item
- A server that already holds the same or a newer edit answers straight away without fetching anything
- Server Sync is a metadata and image provider for every media type. Enable it in a library's metadata and image fetchers to fill new items from the servers it pulls from
- Content and Metadata scans read only what changed on each server. A full scan runs every 24 hours, set by Full Scan Every under Processing
- Peer status reads need the asking server's id and its pairing
- Removed unused API routes

## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## Developer
- A hint is applied only when the item's own path on the origin is inside a mapped library, not just the path the hint names
- Server Sync does not follow redirects from another server. A redirect is reported with the address to use instead
- Plain http:// only reaches loopback, private network, and Tailscale addresses. A server on the public internet needs https://
- Any signed in user's key can pair, so a peer held with a standard user's key pairs like any other
- A peer that cannot pair has its hints refused instead of being taken on its word
- When one server holds a standard user's key for the other, both need this version to pair

## Developer
- Only changes to items in a mapped library, and watch history for mapped users, are queued for a peer. Everything else is dropped before it gathers, so it is never checked or sent

## Developer
- The Queue view's warning about local changes that matched no mapping has a Dismiss button, and saving the configuration checks those changes again so a newly mapped library or user sends them
- Processing settings set how hints are retried. A peer that cannot be reached is tried again after 30 seconds, doubling up to an hour, and a peer that refuses waits 15 minutes. Each has a max retries setting, where 0 keeps trying forever
- The Sync page opens on the Queue when no sync module is enabled, instead of an empty page

## Developer
- Built on base 2026.10.6, which now owns the database's schema version, its oldest reader marker, and setting an unreadable database aside
- A database set aside because a newer version wrote it is kept as a .newer backup instead of a .corrupt one, and the three newest of each are kept
- Activity log entries are written through the base package's logger

## Developer
- The five Sync tables are built from one shared module, so a fix to the table, its buttons, or its modals reaches every view at once
- The refresh run is split into named steps, with the prune's safety checks gathered in one place
- Every Sync view reloads its counts and health figures when a detail dialog closes, and alerts and empty states read the same across views

## Developer
- A slow or silent peer no longer stops hint delivery until a restart. Peer calls have a deadline that covers the whole answer, connections time out after fifteen seconds, and peers are served in parallel
- Two servers holding the same version with different values settle instead of trading the hint forever, and a server only announces edits it made itself
- A sender whose clock runs a few minutes ahead sees its hints completed instead of resent forever
- Versions only move forward, are written at the moment of a hand made edit, and a scan records the version it read with each value rather than asking the peer again per row
- A failed version read no longer lets a scan overwrite edits made here, and those rows wait for the next scan
- In a pool of three or more, a history base made stale by a third server no longer reverts a newer edit, and both sides record a base when nothing needed to change
- Jellyfin's own housekeeping saves no longer pose as hand made edits, and provider work never replaces an item locked here
- Content hints obey the library's allow and block lists and the watched by all filter, and a downloaded file is no longer announced back to the pool
- The negotiated history base cannot be rolled back by a scan, and moving rows to a higher priority server keeps ignored rows and bases and counts toward the safety limit, judged per server like the prune
- The hidden per module tasks no longer run on schedules of their own
- Removing a server takes effect only once saved, removes the hints it sent, and a slow answer for one server can no longer land in another server's editor
- The stored key and pairing secret are only sent to the address saved on the entry, and IPv4 addresses written as IPv6 are checked as IPv4
- Hint queues are bounded and indexed. A full inbound queue answers busy, hints give up after about a day, sent and failed rows expire after a week, and errored rows are retried daily
- A scheduled run no longer holds hint applies for its whole length, and a backlog drains without waiting between batches
- The Queue view refreshes only when something changed, caches posters, shows at most 200 rows, and resumes refreshing when you come back to the page
- A timeout on one item no longer aborts a whole scheduled run, one server that fails to list no longer stops the others, and one module that fails no longer skips the rest of Sync Information or Sync Content
- A transient error no longer reads as an item, a library page, or a profile image being gone, so it cannot truncate a scan or clear a user's picture
- Replacing a file keeps its NFO, images, and other sidecars, a renamed file on a source is moved instead of downloaded again, and a file still on disk stays tracked when its source item goes
- Free space is measured on the library's own disk, the sign in honors the private network rule, and the address check refuses unspecified and multicast addresses
- Retry errors works for History, Metadata, People, and Users, the dashboard keeps scrolling and refreshing after you come back, and slow answers no longer land in the wrong server or modal
- The database records the oldest version that can read it, so going back to an older version keeps it whenever that version can read it
- Every stored and compared time is read and written as UTC in one place
- Writing an item's cast holds back people hints only during the write, not while its images download
- The sync table shows deletions held for approval and deletions in progress when deletion is set to Enabled
- A hint that could not apply shows as Skipped sync for its name on the Activity page, with a plainer reason when the person does not exist here
- Dead code removed and repeated code shared across the plugin, with docs corrected where they had drifted

## Developer
- A season names its series in the activity log and the queue, as Synced The Show Season 1, instead of Season 1 alone

## Developer
- A peer's version can no longer lie ahead of this server's clock. A hint dated more than five minutes ahead is declined, anything less is read as now, and the version store never holds a future stamp
- Requests that name a sender must prove it. Each server issues the servers it lists a pairing secret over its own connection to them, and a batch, completion, or history negotiation without the right secret answers 428 until the real server pairs, which Check Link and the workers do on their own. A server held with a standard user's key cannot be issued one and is taken on its word, as before
- A completion removes only the reporting peer's own rows
- An entry that disallows private networks now holds a name to the same rule as an address, at save time and on every connection
- The inbound queue keeps at most ten thousand rows per origin, finished ids are capped, and a peer's answer is read up to thirty two megabytes
- Nothing gathers or shows for a kind no Push or Sync server applies, though a hand made edit still records its version, and the ancestor walk that sorts provider images from edits runs only when it decides anything
- An applied episode logs Synced [series] S01E02 with [type] [series] S01E02 - [episode] was updated from [server], activity entries no longer end in a full stop, and provider work applied from a peer's scan writes none
- A pass of metadata hints reads the origin's items in pages of fifty, as the scheduled scan does, instead of one request per hint
- The Queue view shows episodes and videos in a wide frame, and its count cards wrap three then two on a phone

## Developer
- An applied change writes Synced [name]. to the activity log, with [type] [name] was updated from [server]. as the detail
- The duplicate DELETE /ServerSync/Peer/Queue/{id} route is gone. Every route requires an administrator, which a unit test and the integration suite now enforce
- The Queue view is one list. Each change is one row for its whole life with a status chip, Jellyfin's title and poster, the user for watch history, a ticking countdown while it gathers, the summary cards and peers as filters, and a layout that stacks on phones

## Developer
- Every metadata and image change travels, posters included. Provider work from a scan or a refresh is marked, fills in where the other server has recorded no edit, and never replaces a poster or field set by hand. Sync database schema v26
- The Queue view lists the changes still gathering, named, with when each goes out, and its To Send card is now Pending
- An applied change writes [type] [name] was updated to the activity log, with the peer it was triggered from in the detail
- User settings are no longer announced live, since Jellyfin raises no event for policy and configuration changes. The scheduled Sync Information task carries them, and the Users settings say so
- Check Link reads as plain sentences

## Developer
- A server only announces the kinds of change its peer applies, read from the peer's enabled modules every minute; Check Link and each peer's card on the Queue view name them
- Send Changes After, under Settings > Processing, sets how long an item must go untouched before a change is sent to peers, sixty seconds by default; every further edit restarts the wait and one update goes out at the end of it
- History hints honour the receiver's History switch like every other kind
- New library mapping rows start enabled
- The Queue view says when a local change matched no library or user mapping on any Push or Sync server, and names the last one
- A poster or other image uploaded or picked by hand travels as a metadata hint; images a provider fetches during a scan or a refresh are still left to the scheduled task

## Developer
- Targets Jellyfin 12.1
- Several servers, scanned in priority order. The single source migrates into the list
- Server modes Pull, Push, and Sync. Push and Sync send change hints to peers running Server Sync, which pull each change within seconds
- Hints cover watch history, metadata, people, users, and new files. Stored on both ends, retried with backoff, recovered when lost
- Watch history merges three way against the state both servers last agreed on
- Metadata, people, and users resolve on where and when a value was last edited, so the newest edit wins
- Two scheduled tasks, Sync Content and Sync Information, replace the ten. The per module tasks are hidden but still run from the dashboard
- Peer endpoints under /ServerSync/Peer and operator endpoints under /ServerSync/Hints, all behind Jellyfin's RequiresElevation policy
- {'Servers tab rebuilt': 'numbered priority list with reorder, Connection, Authentication, Libraries, and Users steps, API key or sign in, and Check Link judged by direction with a clock skew warning'}
- A standard user's key is recognised and pulls what that user can see, one way
- Queue view on the Sync page, and an activity log line for every concluded hint
- A full REST API section in the README
- Each detail dialog shows which server last edited the item and when
- Removing a server removes the rows tracked from it
- Pending hints capped at ten thousand per peer
- Server names with emoji work in peer requests
- Sync database schema v25
- Docker integration harness under integration/

## Developer
- Items with several backdrops no longer queue on every refresh. Jellyfin stores images without an order, so the same set can come back shuffled on either server. Image sizes are now matched as a set within each image type instead of by position
- Metadata Sync people no longer queue again right after a successful sync. Credits are compared the way Jellyfin stores them, ignoring case and padding on names and roles and collapsing duplicate credits, and the post apply check uses the same comparison as the refresh
- Cast order now carries across. People were being written in alphabetical order, and they are now written in the source billing order. Expect one round of people syncs while existing items pick up the correct order
- People Sync no longer syncs the person name. The name is the match key, so the two sides can only differ by casing, and rewriting it made Jellyfin recreate the person blank. The local person is now found by its id first
- User Sync no longer copies EnableAllFolders, EnableAllChannels, or EnableAllDevices. The id lists they depend on stay local, so copying the switch alone could lock a user out of every library or lift a local restriction

## Developer
- Backdrops now sync as a complete set. When an item or a person differs from the source, this server deletes its whole set for that image type, files included, then downloads every source image back in order. A leftover backdrop file can no longer be re-adopted by the next library scan and reinstate the difference
- People image sync now covers backdrops as well as profile images, so a person carrying several backdrops on the source is tracked and applied instead of being ignored
- Change badges in the Metadata and People detail views now explain themselves. The exact diverging image or field is named, so a badge can no longer disagree with rows that look identical
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- Moved to the unstable Jellyfin SDK so the source server client matches the 12.0 API during pre release testing. The SDK now carries Kiota 2.0, so Microsoft.IO.RecyclableMemoryStream ships with the plugin
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

Features:
- New rule field: Aspect Ratio (under Video). Filter by a video's display
  aspect ratio such as 16:9 or 2.35:1. Comparisons are proportional, so
  "less than 1:1" matches every portrait video and "greater than 1:1" every
  landscape one - no need to list each ratio.
- Live TV Channel media type for smart collections. Group channels from any
  Live TV tuner into a collection with rules such as Name, Tags or Is
  Favorite. Collections only - Jellyfin playlists cannot hold channels
  (#290).
- "Hide when empty" is now "Min Items": a list stays hidden until it holds
  at least that many items, instead of only while it is completely empty.
  Found under Limits next to Max Items, with a matching default in
  Settings. Existing lists keep their current behaviour with no changes
  needed.

Bug Fixes:
- MDBList official list URLs (mdblist.com/lists/official/movies/... and
  .../shows/...) returned no items. They now load, and the JustWatch
  Streaming Charts list keeps the country, period, provider and genre
  filters from the pasted URL (#525).

Full changelog: https://jellyfin-smartlists-plugin.dinsten.se/changelog/stable/

Same plugin as v12.0.1.0 - no functional changes. It exists so that servers
upgraded from Jellyfin 10.11 to Jellyfin 12 automatically pick up the correct
build.

Bug Fixes:
- Upgrading Jellyfin from 10.11 to 12 left the plugin showing "Not supported".
  Each release published its 10.11 and its 12 build under the same version
  number, so a server that had installed the 10.11 build kept it after the
  upgrade - Jellyfin saw no newer version to offer, and the 10.11 build cannot
  run on Jellyfin 12. This release is published for Jellyfin 12 only, so those
  servers now see an update and repair themselves. Jellyfin 10.11 servers are
  unaffected and stay on v12.0.1.0.

Full changelog: https://jellyfin-smartlists-plugin.dinsten.se/changelog/stable/

StarTrack.description: Community star ratings for movies and TV shows — stored privately on your Jellyfin server.
StarTrack.overview: StarTrack adds a compact star rating pill to every Movie and TV Series detail page in your Jellyfin library. Click it to expand a full panel where you can submit your 1-5 star rating and see a breakdown of every individual user's score. All data lives in a JSON file on your server — nothing leaves your network.

versions.changelog: Fixes for 1.8.0, almost all reported by users of it. JELLYFIN 12.1: StarTrack appears in the new Material-UI top bar - 12.1 moved navigation there and the nav drawer the My Ratings link used is not in that layout (#27). FIXES: opening a film from My Ratings no longer freezes page scrolling (six code paths closed the overlay and only one released the scroll lock, leaving the whole web UI unscrollable until a reload) (#27); Back closes My Ratings instead of navigating the page behind it (#27); half stars are cut at the middle of the glyph again (#27); 'out of ten' now applies to your own ratings too, not only community averages - panel, recent list, cards, diary and comparison (#27); Letterboxd 'Verify login' opens its session the way a real push does - it never used FlareSolverr, so a correct server still failed it, and a stale pasted cookie was used forever and never questioned, which is worse than none - it now retries without your cookies and on a fresh challenge and says what actually fixes a Cloudflare block (#24); the self-check no longer reports a failure for a read-only index.html, the normal state in Docker, on a server that is injecting perfectly well by its other route (#20); a duplicate copy of a film in the library no longer collects a second rating on import. NEW: StarTrack tells you when your browser is running a cached old copy of it, with a Reload button, and never reloads on its own (#20); a My Ratings button in the rating panel (#28); remove from watchlist directly from the watchlist (#28).

Jellyfin 12 support from one codebase: two builds, 1.8.0.0 for 10.11 and 1.8.0.1 for 12; the catalogue picks the right one. LETTERBOXD: 'Sync everything' imports your whole profile live - every rating including films rated but never logged, every dated diary entry, then watchlist, likes and Top 4 - with never-logged films placed in the order you rated them; watchlist sync works again (Letterboxd removed the RSS feed, the page is read instead); likes, Top 4 and sign-in get through Cloudflare via an optional FlareSolverr, and back off politely with a visible note without one; imports never overwrite reviews or dates they do not carry; a known year is a matching constraint (Fall 2022 is not The Fall 2006); duplicate library copies rate the one you already rated; likes are dated by the viewing, not the import. DIARY: one viewing, one row - a playback row and its later rating merge (timezone-safe); pre-rolls and trailers under two minutes are not logged; a rating from any source fills an unrated row. RATINGS: admin choice of stars, stars+/10, or /10 everywhere an average shows (display only); IMDb ratings CSV import, auto-detected; IMDb/Yamtrack export reports what it left out. SIMKL: pull converges (#19) - any shared id matches. FIXES: tick boxes hidden by global CSS themes; poster badges fetched in one batch instead of one request per card; settings-load failures say so instead of showing everything unticked. NEW: 'Is StarTrack working?' self-check with a paste-ready report. Everything translated in all 8 languages.

versions.changelog:
Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12.

Adgangsnøglen: Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende den på (X-Emby-Token). Det ramte Subtitle Guard hårdere end de andre plugins — tolv forskellige kald sendte den gamle vej, og de svarede alle 401 på Jellyfin 12. I praksis betød det at alt det der foregår fra selve siden holdt op med at virke: workers, køen, historikken, knapperne på detaljesiden. Alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt.

Indstillingssiden kunne slet ikke åbnes på Jellyfin 12. Pluginet kørte, men dets side under Dashboard → Plugins var der ikke, og der stod ingen fejl nogen steder. Det er den side hvor workers tilmeldes, så uden den kunne en ny worker ikke sættes op. Jellyfin 12's nye dashboard viser kun siden, hvis den selv beder om at komme i menuen.

Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan kun installeres der. Kører du stadig 10.11, bliver du på 2.1.0.0, som virker uændret — serveren vælger selv den rigtige. Grunden til at der skal være to: 10.11 og 12 kører på hver sin udgave af .NET, så det samme build kan ikke køre begge steder.

Bemærk: selve sync-workeren er urørt. Den kører for sig selv og er ikke berørt af hvilken Jellyfin-version serveren har.

versions.changelog: - The events endpoint now requires an administrator or an API key on both Jellyfin and Emby.

- Jellyfin builds now target .NET 10 against the Jellyfin 12.0 plugin ABI. Jellyfin 12 moved the server to .NET 10 and changed several plugin interfaces, so a 10.11 build does not load on it. Catalog entries carry `targetAbi` 12.0.0.0, which hides them from 10.11 servers; 0.4.1 stays the last release for 10.11.
- Emby is unaffected. `Emby.Plugin.Sse` is still netstandard2.0 and still targets Emby 4.9+.

## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## Features
- Groups can now manage whether members may change their own display and playback preferences
- Groups can now manage the sync transcoding and public sharing permissions
- Groups can now manage whether a Collections view is shown on the home screen

## Fixes
- A deleted user is dropped from group membership and enrollment records the moment the server deletes them, rather than on the next save or sync

## Developer
- Remove the unused HasPassword override. Jellyfin 12 dropped it from IAuthenticationProvider and performs that check itself, so the method was dead code the server never called

## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

VideoOSD Tweaks and Candy.description: VideoOSD Tweaks and Candy turns the Jellyfin video player OSD into your personal control center. Hide or reorder any vanilla OSD element across all four zones independently, full freedom over every detail. Eight optional addons extend the OSD with features you know from VLC and beyond: a Custom On/Off Menu for quick in-playback switching, Playback Speed Buttons and a Speed Menu with your own custom speed values directly in the OSD, Frame-by-Frame Buttons, a Download Button, a Screenshot Button, and an A-B Loop Button. And then there is the Candy: Artwork Display upgrades the OSD to a whole new level, fully configurable down to the smallest detail with logos, clearart, discs, posters, banners, thumbs, and backdrops, each artwork type separately configurable for movies, episodes, and videos. All addons are optional and configurable through the Jellyfin admin dashboard.

versions.changelog:
This update brings together 2.0.10.0 and 2.0.11.0 from the beta channel.

If you use the Live TV allow-list behind a reverse proxy: add the proxy to Known Proxies in Jellyfin's networking settings. Without that, every request through the proxy counts as coming from the proxy, and if its address is on your list, everyone gets in. The help text now says so.

Fixed: with Live TV set up on two or more providers, the guide never used your providers' XMLTV files. They were combined into one file that could not be read past the first provider, so the guide always fell back to the simpler per-channel listings and lost categories, ratings and the other details XMLTV carries. Each provider's file is now read on its own. If one provider's file is missing or broken, only that provider's channels fall back, and the others keep their full guide (found and fixed by dillardblom).

Fixed: when two providers used the same guide id for different channels, one of them got no guide, or showed the other provider's programmes. Guide ids are now matched per provider (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: when your provider's XMLTV guide came through cut off part way, building the guide never finished. Each request for the EPG URL kept one CPU core busy until Jellyfin gave up, and the guide stayed empty. A broken file now falls back to fetching the guide per channel, as it already did when the file was missing, and no programme is listed twice (by dillardblom).

Fixed: with Dispatcharr mode on, every sync worker logged in to Dispatcharr at the same time when a sync started. Dispatcharr's login limit refused most of them, and those workers fell back to the Xtream API for the first minutes. There is now one login shared by all of them, and it waits its turn like every other request (reported by dillardblom).

This update brings together 2.0.2.0 to 2.0.9.0 from the beta channel.

If you use Live TV with the Native Tuner only, open the Live TV tab after updating and turn off the new "Publish Playlists" switch. It stays on for anyone who already had Live TV enabled, so an M3U tuner or TiviMate setup keeps working, but the native tuner does not need it.

Fixed: Request Delay now limits how fast the plugin talks to your provider in total. Each parallel worker used to apply it separately, so with Sync Parallelism at 10 and the default of 50 ms up to 200 requests a second could go out, enough for some providers to block your IP. It is now one shared gap per provider: 50 ms means at most 20 a second. When the provider says it is getting too many requests, every request to it waits. A first sync of a large library takes longer as a result; if your provider allows more, lower Request Delay. Setting it to 0 is no longer saved as 50 (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: a single unreadable value from your provider, such as an empty value where a number belongs, no longer makes content disappear. It could blank a series' title, plot and TMDB id, drop every episode of a series, or make a whole category fail to sync. Such values are now ignored or read as 0, and an item whose ID cannot be read is skipped with a warning while the rest syncs normally (reported by foXaCe).

Fixed: changing Folder Mode, or moving a category to another folder, no longer leaves every moved item in your library twice. The old copies are removed even beyond the orphan safety limit, as long as the item only moved to another category folder; anything that actually disappeared is still protected by the limit. Moved items lose their watched status, because Jellyfin sees a new folder as a new item (reported in andreadegiovine's fork).

Fixed: when orphan cleanup removes a movie or series, the NFO and poster the plugin wrote are removed with it, so the folder no longer stays behind. Files you added yourself, such as subtitles or your own NFO, are kept, and so is the folder (idea from andreadegiovine).

Fixed: with "Group movies with the same TMDB id" on, a film whose request the provider missed no longer ends up in a folder of its own. It is held back and picked up on the next sync. Films already split this way stay split; to fix them, use Delete Movies Library in the Danger Zone and sync again (reported by andreadegiovine).

New: with "Fallback to Year-Free Lookup" on, an unmatched movie is also searched with the year of the provider's release date and with its original title, which helps when the title carries the wrong year or is in another language. A search without a year is checked against the release date, so it cannot pick a remake. A match found by the year-free retry is now remembered for later syncs, for movies and series. Movies already in your library keep their folders (idea from philx17).

New: "Publish Playlists" on the Live TV tab. The M3U and Catch-up M3U URLs contain your Xtream username and password and can be reached without a Jellyfin login. They are now only served while this switch is on, and it is off when you enable Live TV from now on. The EPG URL and channel logos are not affected (proposed by dillardblom).

New: "Restrict These URLs To" limits the Live TV URLs to the addresses you list, one per line. Leave it empty for no restriction. If you use it, include 127.0.0.1 and ::1, since Jellyfin fetches channel logos itself, and behind a reverse proxy add the proxy to Known Proxies in Jellyfin's networking settings first (written by dillardblom).

Fixed: a Live TV category, channel or logo address with & in it no longer shows as & or breaks (reported by TheBazeman).

Categories load their items again on Jellyfin 12 (#117).

Jellyfin 12 stops accepting the legacy `X-Emby-Token` request header. Two of the configuration page fetch sites still sent it: the Live TV category loader and the Series / VOD content loader. Both now send `Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=` instead, which Jellyfin 12's `CustomAuthentication` middleware expects. The Test connection button was never affected and still works as before. Two-line header swap in `config.js`, no server-side change.

versions.changelog:
## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## Features
- Replace a library song's audio with a different YouTube upload from the Download tab; it keeps the song's file, tags, cover and playlist places.
- Choosing an album already in the library on the Import tab takes that album's cover.
- Imports join existing artist and album folders whose names differ only in case, punctuation or year, and take that album's name and year.

## Features
- Republishes 12.2.3.0, whose download did not match its checksum and could not install.

## Features
- Import Spotify playlists exported with Exportify, one playlist as CSV or all of them as a ZIP.
- Spotify imports embed Spotify's album cover and fill in the genre from Apple Music.
- Playlist tracks with an ISRC are matched to their official YouTube upload by it first.
- Generate a cover with the wand button on the Import tab; choose its text, order and colors in Settings → Album Art.
- Composer credits are stored as separate composers.
- Live, remix, cover, acoustic and instrumental versions are never matched unless the song's title names that version.

## Features
- When Apple Music has no cover, the album cover from the official YouTube Music track is used.
- Re-pitched, sped-up, 8D and nightcore uploads are never matched.
- Artists YouTube Music credits in another alphabet (such as Cyrillic) are matched by album or exact length.
- Re-importing a playlist removes queued or failed songs your library now has.

## Features
- YouTube matches must contain the song title, so another song by the same artist with a similar length is never downloaded instead.
- Importing rescans only the imported songs' folders instead of the whole library.

## Features
- Look up each download on Apple Music to fill in its title, album, album artist, year, track number and genre (Settings, on by default).
- Embed the album cover from Apple Music in downloaded files (Settings, on by default).
- Upload your own cover art on the Import tab, for one file or all selected files.
- Songs already in your library are marked Already in your library on the Import tab.
- Joint artist credits are stored as separate artists, and new imports reuse the library's spelling of an artist.
- Playlist imports use the album's release date for its year.
- Playlist tracks the regular YouTube search cannot match are looked up in YouTube Music's song results.

## Features
- Change the YouTube link of any queued track from its queue row, keeping its details and playlist.
- Better matching for classical tracks, and uploads by other performers are no longer picked.
- Classical tracks already in your library are recognized even when tagged with only the movement name (or only the full work title), so they are not downloaded again.

## Features
- Preview downloaded tracks on the Import tab before importing them.
- Genres are capitalized, split into separate genres, and standardized (for example alt-pop becomes Alternative and Pop).

## Features
- Import Apple Music playlists (text or XML export) and whole library exports; each track is matched to a YouTube upload at download time.
- Imported playlists become private Jellyfin playlists for a chosen user, filled as songs reach the library, appended to and re-ordered when one of the same name exists.
- Import cleanup groups album editions (Deluxe, Remastered, Bonus Track…), moves feat. artists into tags, skips songs already in the library or queue, and upgrades library singles to the album version.
- Public read-only queue page at /YouTube/Queue for signed-in users.
- yt-dlp and the Deno runtime it needs for YouTube are downloaded automatically, yt-dlp is kept up to date, and downloads YouTube temporarily refuses are retried.
- Failed queue items can be retried from the Download tab.

## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs
